☆ Quantitative constructive representation of the KdV flow in $H^3$ via $L^2$-energy-preserving centered-difference Chernoff approximations and Picard iteration
Comlan Edmond Koudjinan
We give a constructive representation of the solution of the KdV equation $u_t=-u_{xxx}+6uu_x$ on $\mathbb R$ for real initial data in $H^3(\mathbb R)$. The approximations couple an exact, unitary centered-difference Chernoff product for the Airy group with a skew-symmetric discretization of the quadratic term, and are computed by Picard iteration; they preserve the $L^2$ norm exactly, as does the limit. A two-mesh Cauchy argument shows that the whole sequence converges in $C([0,T];H^2)$, at rate $O(n^{-\frac{2(s-2)}5})$ for $H^s$ data ($3\leq s\leq 7$), and in $L^2$ at rate $O(n^{-6/5})$ for $H^3$ data. This scheme, to the best of our knowledge, is novel and is of independent interest. As a by-product we obtain existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, Lipschitz dependence on the data in the $H^2$ norm, uniformly on bounded subsets of $H^3$ and compact time intervals, and joint locally Lipschitz dependence of $(t,f)\mapsto S(t)f$ into $L^2$; the classical conservation laws extend the flow globally in time.

☆ Non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation
Mikaela Iacobelli
We prove non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation on the whole space. More precisely, for every finite $p$, we construct a nonnegative ion density, smooth for positive times, and a source $S\in C([0,1];L^1(\R^2))$ with $S(0)=0$, for which there exist two distinct nonnegative distributional solutions $f_\pm\in C([0,1];L^1(\R^2))$ with the same zero initial datum and with spatial densities bounded in $L^p(\R)$ uniformly in time. The result is sharp in terms of the integrability of the spatial densities: our solutions have Lipschitz electric fields, and we show that in this class uniqueness holds as soon as the spatial density is bounded.
☆ SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
Viktor Stein, Levin Maier, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl
The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood. Recent perspectives interpret attention blocks as interacting particle systems, whose mean-field limits correspond to gradient flows of energy functionals on spaces of probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with Wasserstein-type metrics. We extend this viewpoint by deriving accelerated attention blocks from inertial, Nesterov-type damped Hamiltonian dynamics on these density spaces, developing the geometry and differential calculus needed to make the construction rigorous. In particular, we introduce a local-mobility geometry for the Otto-Wasserstein and softmax-Wasserstein settings, and a quotient Stein geometry that resolves the degeneracy of the linear-attention kernel to yield a well-defined metric and differential calculus. We provide rigorous foundations when softmax attention admits a gradient-flow formulation and when its inertial counterpart admits a damped Hamiltonian on explicitly characterized domains. For linear attention, we obtain a finite-dimensional solution theory with sharp conditions for global existence versus finite-time second-moment blow-up. We further prove a quantitative link between continuous moment blow-up and the discrete-layer depth at which token norms cross a prescribed threshold. Finally, motivated by the finite-token geometry, we propose geometric corrections to token and momentum updates. In decoder-only, nanoGPT-style experiments on TinyStories and OpenWebText, these corrections lower validation negative log-likelihood on next-token prediction relative to momentum-only controls.

☆ Sharp fractional Hardy--Maz'ya remainders on half-spaces: angular reduction and energy stability
Shengbing Deng, Dehong Yang
For $d\geq2$, $01$, and $τ>0$, we study the sharp half-space remainder \[ [u]_{s,p,+}^p-\mathcal D_{d,s,p}\int_{\mathbb R^d_+}x_d^{-sp}|u|^p\,dx \geqΛ_{d,s,p,τ}\int_{\mathbb R^d_+} \frac{x_d^{τ-sp}|u|^p}{(x_{d-1}^2+x_d^2)^{τ/2}}\,dx. \] We first obtain exact dimensional and angular reductions by an $L^p$ contraction. For $p=2$, we identify the planar sharp coefficient with the simple first eigenvalue of a singular angular operator with compact resolvent. We prove a ground-state representation and a two-sided estimate for the sharp deficit. These give quantitative stability and a Fourier--Mellin energy criterion for extremizing sequences in all dimensions. For the distance with multiplier $h(ξ)=\min\{ξ^2,1\}$, the best planar stability coefficient is not attained and is strictly smaller than the quadratic dispersion coefficient. The minimizing frequencies are nonzero when $τ=2$ and $s$ is close to one. Finally, we prove normalized local limits for the sharp quadratic constant, each fixed fiber eigenvalue, and the dispersion coefficient.
☆ A Sharp Gradient Harnack Estimate for the Lane--Emden System
Sanghoon Lee, Kui Li, Juncheng Wei
We establish a sharp pointwise gradient estimate for positive entire classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system when one of the exponents lies below the Serrin exponent $n/(n-2)$. The estimate generalizes the positivity of the scalar curvature of the associated conformal metric in the biharmonic case $q=1$. The coefficient in the estimate is optimal on the critical hyperbola.

☆ Boltzmann Equation and Hard Sphere Gas with Singular Initial Data: Well-posedness, Kinetic Limit, and Weak Stability
Chenjiayue Qi
We develop a local well-posedness theory for the spatially inhomogeneous 3-d Boltzmann equation with hard sphere cross-section, accommodating a class of large initial data. This class is an interpolation between the space $L_{x}^{\infty}L_v^{1}$ and $L_{v}^1L_{x}^{\infty}$ (with weight in $v$). It is notable for including data that can have infinite $L_{x,v}^\infty$-norm, entropy density. The core idea of the proof is a homogenization method based on collision geometries. As a key application, we prove the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with initial data in this space, having certain extra conditions. This is the first proof on the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with singular initial data. We also derive weak stability estimates of Boltzmann equation and hard sphere gas within the same functional spaces.
☆ A sharpened $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate for even initial data
Soichiro Suzuki
It is well known that $u_0 \in L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ is an extremizer for the $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate if and only if it is a Gaussian. We show that every extremizing sequence of even functions $\{ u_n \} \subset L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ approaches a centered Gaussian in an appropriate sense. This result follows from a certain inequality for coordinate-wise even $L^2$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^4$ conjectured by Gonçalves (2019) which we prove in this paper with the optimal constant.

☆ A spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
Konstantin Merz
We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a Hörmander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sjöstrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.

☆ Liouville-type theorems and perturbation uniqueness for stationary incompressible MHD with directional fractional dissipation
Yong Zeng
We study Liouville-type theorems for stationary solutions of the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with directional fractional dissipation $(-\partial_i^2)^αu$ and $(-\partial_j^2)^βb$, where $n\ge 2$ and $0<α,β\le 1$. We prove that $u\equiv b\equiv 0$ by assuming that $u\in L^{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $b\in L^{q,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, with suitable conditions on $p$ and $q$. The proof uses a localized fractional energy identity and does not assume finiteness of the global homogeneous Sobolev energy. The method also applies to the case of full fractional dissipation. For the system with common-directional fractional dissipation, we prove stationary uniqueness for compactly supported perturbations of arbitrary smooth transverse shear backgrounds when $0<α,β<1$. We also establish a quantitative uniqueness criterion for perturbations of backgrounds with bounded gradients that are not necessarily compactly supported, for all $0<α,β\le 1$, assuming directional localization.

☆ Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
Pascal Hadré, Richard M. Höfer
In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2ε$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_ε$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_ε$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_ε$ and $b_ε$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.

☆ Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves I: The disc
Shengquan Xiang
Building on the spacetime observable symmetry discovered in NWX (2025), we introduce asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) for the wave equation. Its central object is a family of generated approximate velocities constructed from fixed profiles, carrying the same propagation-induced symmetry at different scales and asymptotically realized by exact waves. We investigate AOS on the disc through radial propagation and reflection. This gives a family of spacetime measurable observation sets satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition for a fixed positive observation time. However, the observability inequality fails on each of these fixed sets.
☆ Pólya's conjecture for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells
Yutian Li
We prove the strict Pólya inequality for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$, for every radius ratio and every positive energy. The proof also covers balls. For shells, the excess over the leading Weyl term has a positive lower bound depending only on dimension. Above explicit frequency thresholds independent of the radius ratio, we obtain a surplus of boundary order. These estimates remain uniform as the hole shrinks or the shell becomes thin. We compare weighted sampling errors for inverse radial actions while retaining the removed volume exactly. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted verification.

☆ Uniform coarse ellipticity, $A_2$ weights, and boundary regularity
Kaj Nyström
We study symmetric divergence form elliptic equations with measurable coefficients that may be degenerate and unbounded, under a uniform bound on the coarse ellipticity ratio over all ambient cubes and scales. We prove that uniform coarse ellipticity and classical $A_2$ weighted ellipticity define incomparable coefficient classes. For every admissible choice of coarse parameters, we construct a scalar weight with a logarithmically corrected, locally integrable singularity along a product Cantor set. Its codimension is chosen according to the upper coarse discount exponent, and the resulting coefficient satisfies the uniform coarse condition but is comparable to no $A_2$ weight. Conversely, an explicit $A_2$ weight fails the coarse condition for every admissible parameter choice. Under uniform coarse ellipticity we give a direct PDE treatment of boundary regularity in the approximable energy realization. Using coarse interior estimates, we prove boundary decay and solvability of the continuous Dirichlet problem in bounded NTA domains. An almost-positivity argument, with energy approximation and boundary testing justified, yields boundary Harnack and Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions with common zero boundary values. The argument requires no additional energy Sobolev inequality and avoids the construction of Green functions. Further examples distinguish uniform coarse control from finite coefficient moments and from coercivity on $\mathrm L^2(\mathrm{d} x)$. We also record interior Hölder estimates and continuity criteria under nonuniform control along nested scales.
☆ On exact solutions to three-dimensional Yukawa lattice model and BCC to FCC phase transitions
Senping Luo, Juncheng Wei
We determine the global minimizers of the three-dimensional Yukawa lattice energy at every fixed density. At unit covolume, BCC is the unique minimizer below a transition parameter $κ_*\approx1.7179218684699$, FCC is the unique minimizer above it, and exactly these two lattice classes minimize at the transition. Mathematically, denote the Yukawa potential and the energy per particle under this potential by \[ v_κ(r)=\frac{e^{-κr}}r,\qquad E_κ(L)=\frac12\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}} \frac{e^{-κ|v|}}{|v|}. \] Then, \[ \arg\min_{|L|=1}E_κ(L)= \begin{cases} \hbox{BCC lattice},&0<κ<κ_*, \hbox{BCC or FCC lattice},&κ=κ_*, \hbox{FCC lattice},&κ>κ_*. \end{cases} \] As a consequence, the zero-screening comparison recovers the unique BCC minimum for the renormalized Coulomb energy.

☆ A special Hardy estimate in the axisymmetric swirl problem
Daoguo Zhou
We examine the proof of Dongyi Wei's logarithmic circulation criterion. A trace estimate specific to $\nabla(u_r/r)$ replaces a generic squared-swirl form bound by one with one logarithm rather than two. Repeating the coupled $J$--$Ω$ energy and comparison argument then gives a proposed threshold of order $(\log D)^{-5/4}$. ☆ A hybrid finite-volume scheme with learned rational reconstructions and exact nonlocal fluxes for the space-fractional Burgers equation
Zeyuan Song, Zheyu Jiang
On coarse grids, fronts of fractional conservation laws can be narrower than one cell, while the flux through each face depends on the whole domain. For the forced space-fractional Burgers equation, we write the finite-volume defect exactly, with the Riesz flux acting as a nonlocal interface flux. Our proposed closure, NRC, is decoder-only, since the encoder is the exact cell-average projection and a small network only maps cell averages to a sub-cell reconstruction. The decoder adds rational atoms with learned complex poles to a trigonometric histopolant, preserves every cell average, and has closed-form advective and Riesz fluxes. We prove that the scheme conserves mass for every value of the weights and that the learned sub-grid flux has a dipole tail. On 64 cells, NRC reaches a median test error of 0.0308% over three seeds, against 0.431% for WENO5-Z and 0.153% for a black-box flux correction. Ablations show that the exact global operator, the projection and the sub-grid Riesz flux carry most of this gain, and most sub-cell fronts carry a deep learned pole within a quarter cell. NRC keeps its advantage over WENO5-Z under shifts of the order and the forcing and, when trained on several diffusivities, under the tested diffusivity shifts by factors from 0.6 to 2.5 in the median over seeds. From 32 to 128 cells, NRC stays an order of magnitude more accurate than WENO5-Z on the same grid. This gain lies in accuracy per degree of freedom and in an interpretable closure.

☆ Concavity of the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck torsion function on centered ellipses and its failure on convex domains
Xuan Hien Nguyen, Alina Stancu
Let $u$ be the torsion function of a bounded domain $Ω$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, that is, the solution of $-Δu + x\cdot\nabla u = 1$ in $Ω$ with $u=0$ on the boundary. We prove that for every $n\ge2$ there are bounded, centrally symmetric domains whose torsion function is not concave. These domains have boundary with a flat piece and can be smoothed so that the boundary is $C^\infty$, strictly convex with principal curvatures bounded below by a positive constant, while keeping the torsion function not concave. In contrast, the torsion function for every ellipse centered at the origin is concave, and for every ball centered at the origin we prove the sharp bound $D^2u\leq-\frac{1}{n}I$. The ellipse result follows by deformation from the disk, using a boundary flux estimate and third-order boundary identities to exclude a first zero eigenvalue of the Hessian.

☆ Lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions for a class of curvilinear polygons
Jeffrey Galkowski, Ruoyu P. T. Wang
Steklov eigenfunctions, $\{φ_{σ_j}\}_{j=0}^\infty$, are the eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet to Neumann map on a bounded domain with eigenvalue $σ_j$. This paper considers Steklov eigenfunctions and eigenvalues on a family of curvilinear polygons, $Ω_α$ whose boundaries are smooth away from a single corner of angle $α$. We (i) prove optimal lower bounds on the decay of the harmonic extension, $u_{σ_j}$, of $φ_{σ_j}$ away from the boundary of $Ω_α$ and (ii) give optimal lower bounds on the degree to which the high energy Steklov spectrum of $Ω_α\setminus H_1$ may differ from that of $Ω_α\setminus H_0$ when $H_1$ and $H_0$ are isometric. This shows that the corresponding estimates in recent work by the authors together with Malagutti are optimal. The proof in this paper was obtained through an interaction with ChatGPT 6 Astra: While writing the work with Malagutti, the authors became curious about optimal error bounds for the difference between the Steklov spectra on a curvilinear polygon, $P$, and the spectrum of any operator which knows only local information about $\partial P$. The authors suggested to ChatGPT to remove two isometric, smooth domains from a curvilinear polygon. ChatGPT suggested the ideas for a proof based on a regularized trace and the singularity in the kernel of the DtN map near a corner. The authors then suggested a simpler, conformal approach, the method for handling small angles, and the idea to obtain lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions. The paper is entirely written by the authors and the argument has been significantly modified, clarified, and simplified from the ChatGPT ideas.
☆ Sharp stability for the Talenti inequality
Paolo Acampora, Jimmy Lamboley, Idriss Mazari-Fouquer
We prove a sharp quantitative version of the Talenti rearrangement inequality. Specifically, we show that, for any $p\in [1;+\infty]$, for any $f\in L^\infty(Ω),\, f\geq 0,\, f\not\equiv 0$, for any open set $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with finite volume, the solution $u_{f,Ω}$ to $-Δu_{f,Ω}=f,\, u_{f,Ω} \in W^{1,2}_0(Ω)$, satisfies, in dimension $d\geq 1$, $\Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ and, in dimension 1, $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ where $α(Ω)$ denotes the Fraenkel asymmetry of $Ω$, $\mathscr A(f,z)$ a weighted asymmetry of $f$ with respect to some center $z$ and $Ω^\sharp$ (resp. $f^\sharp$) is the Schwarz rearrangement of $Ω$ (resp. of $f$). In dimension $d\geq 2$, this estimate implies $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\Vert f-f^\sharp(\cdot-z)\Vert_{L^1}^2.$ Our result sharpens and extends recent quantitative versions, and does not rely on shape differentiation arguments, but on a generalisation of the quantitative Saint-Venant inequality.
☆ Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
Xi Chen, Kuangmiao Xiong, Boxi Xu
We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_1$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.

☆ Continuation and convergence for the higher dimensional conformal Chern--Calabi flow
Hongyu Chen, Li Ma, Li Sheng
We study the volume-normalized gradient flow of the squared Chern scalar curvature on compact Hermitian manifolds of complex dimension $n\ge3$. The flow extends smoothly past a finite time if the spatial supremum of Chern scalar curvature belongs to $L^2$ in time. A uniform curvature bound in the evolving $L^p$ norm, for one fixed $p>n$, gives global existence and smooth convergence of the whole trajectory to a constrained critical metric. On Chern scalar-flat backgrounds, small initial $L^p$ curvature gives exponential convergence to the background. A corresponding condition on the trace-free first Chern--Ricci form gives exponential convergence on Chern--Ricci-flat Hermitian and positive Kähler--Einstein backgrounds. The smallness thresholds are independent of the initial higher derivatives. We also construct constant Chern scalar curvature backgrounds of either sign with arbitrarily small smooth perturbations whose solutions, if global, cannot converge back to the background.

We achieve this result by first defining the measure $ρ^+_δ[λ]$ on the shell $\{δ\le |x| \le 1\}$, $0 < δ< 1$, with a boundary condition on the sphere of radius $δ$ of the form $u|_{\{|x| = δ\}} = λ$. Then we prove that this measure satisfies a variational formula, and use it to show moment bounds which are uniform in the boundary value $λ$. A crucial ingredient in this argument is the fact that every solution of the elliptic equation $-Δu + u^3 = 0$ on the annulus $\{ δ\le |x| \le 1 \}$ satisfies uniform bounds inside the domain, independently of the boundary conditions.

☆ A New Minimax Theorem for a Class of $C^1$-Functionals
Denilson S. Pereira, João R. Santos Júnior, João F. F. Silva
We establish a new abstract minimax theorem for obtaining ground-state critical points of a class of \(C^{1}\)-functionals. The central feature of this class is that the associated Nehari set is not necessarily a differentiable manifold, but is homeomorphic to a (possibly non-complete) submanifold of the unit sphere. This occurs for functionals whose fibering maps \(t \mapsto I(tu)\) possess a unique global maximum point only when \(u\) belongs to an open cone in the underlying Banach space. A lower semicontinuous boundary barrier, which may be finite, controls minimizing sequences near the boundary of the spherical cone. As a consequence, we provide a general minimax characterization of the ground-state energy level. Elliptic applications complement existing results and include superlinear and quasilinear problems with finite barriers, including thresholds depending on the profile of a first eigenfunction and its gradient.

☆ Chaos of Caputo derivative
El-Mahdi Nafia, Aziz El Ghazouani, M'hamed El Omari
We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fréchet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.
☆ Sparse power spectrum for passive scalars under Pierrehumbert flow
Alex Blumenthal, William Cooperman
We study the long-time Fourier distribution of driven passive scalars transported by an incompressible alternating shear flow (the Pierrehumbert flow) subjected to IID random phase shifts, in the regime of strong shear-strength. With a novel and self-contained proof, we establish (i) a quantitative version of the cumulative Batchelor's law; (ii) quantitative negative regularity mixing estimates; and (iii) a strong form of `sparsity' -- unevenness in the distribution of Fourier mass in radial sectors in frequency space. Our method uses the strong shear-strength assumption to handle a purely deterministic scalar driving term.

☆ Exact controllability and rapid stabilization of linear difference delay equations and one-dimensional hyperbolic systems
Yacine Chitour, Sébastien Fueyo, Pierre Lissy, Guilherme Mazanti
This paper addresses exact controllability and rapid stabilization issues for linear difference delay systems with finitely many pointwise delays. We first establish a criterion for exact controllability in $L^r$, $r \in [1, +\infty)$, characterized by a necessary and sufficient Hautus-type frequency-domain condition. The sufficiency of this condition in $L^r$ was already known [https://hal.science/hal-04830757/], whereas its necessity had previously been established only in $L^1$ [arXiv:2210.13590]. We answer [arXiv:2210.13590, Conjecture 3.8] by proving that this condition is also necessary for $r \in (1, +\infty)$. The analysis is based on rewriting the system as an evolution equation in a suitable Banach space, which allows one to apply duality arguments in the spirit of [https://doi.org/10.1137/S036301299119795X]. Building on this controllability analysis and the abstract stabilization framework developed in [https://doi.org/10.1137/S0363012996301609, arXiv:1301.5744], we prove that our exact controllability criterion in $L^r$ is also a sufficient condition for rapid stabilization in $L^2$, i.e., that the system of interest can be stabilized by a family of state feedback control laws ensuring that the closed-loop system is exponentially stable in $L^2$ with an arbitrarily large decay rate. As an application, we extend our results to linear one-dimensional hyperbolic partial differential equations, which can be reduced to linear difference delay systems via the method of characteristics, obtaining also a necessary and sufficient frequency-domain criterion for exact controllability in $L^r$, $r\in [1, +\infty)$, which, as before, is a sufficient condition for rapid stabilization in $L^2$.
☆ Sharp quantitative stability of the Ashbaugh--Benguria inequality
Long-Han Huang, Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou
We establish sharp quantitative stability of the Ashbaugh--Benguria inequality on bounded convex domains in $\mathbb R^n$. After volume and centroid normalization, the eigenvalue-ratio deficit controls the squared $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb S^{n-1})$ norm of the radial displacement from the unit sphere. This yields the optimal exponent $5/2$ for the Fraenkel asymmetry and, for small deficits, the optimal exponent $(n+4)/2$ for the normalized Hausdorff distance. All three exponents are sharp even among smooth strictly convex domains whose principal curvatures lie in $[1/2,2]$. In particular, the quadratic Fraenkel-asymmetry estimate proposed by Brasco and De Philippis (2017, Open Problem 7.65) fails. We also determine the optimal stability exponents under higher-order radial regularity bounds.

The radial kernel is nonincreasing and satisfies $K(r)\asymp r^{ρ-n}$. The coefficients satisfy $0n-ρ+\varepsilon_K, \] where the defects bound the radial logarithmic derivatives. No symmetry, finite-energy condition, or prescribed decay is assumed. The proof combines a localized virial identity with a source-layer pressure estimate whose constants are uniform under centered dilations, including the low-order range $0<ρ\le1$. We also identify the necessary scaling range for existence. For radial weighted Newton systems with unequal powers, we prove that the combined coefficient defect has a sharp, unattained infimum equal to the subcritical gap. A fixed bound on the coefficient ratios forces a strictly larger defect, whereas suitable coefficient--solution pairs approach the threshold with excess at most $C/\log M$. In the scalar Newton case, the threshold is explicit and the approximating family converges, after normalization, to an explicit critical weighted profile. The sharpness results concern the Newton kernel; no corresponding construction is asserted for general fractional kernels.

The eigenfunctions consist of homogeneous Grushin-harmonic polynomials of degrees $n \equiv 0,1 \pmod{α+1}$, even and odd in the $x$-variable respectively, which can be described in terms of Jacobi polynomials.

These results extend a corresponding local strong and classical solvability theory developed for the underlying system without the stress variable $g$ to the present, stress-augmented setting.

We therefore work in analytic function spaces, realized as exponentially weighted hybrid Besov spaces, and develop a global-in-time analytic framework based on Littlewood--Paley analysis and uniform-in-\(τ\) energy estimates. A key ingredient is the introduction of the kinematic stress tensor, which allows us to establish the required a priori estimates in hybrid Besov spaces. Based on these estimates, we prove the existence of a unique global-in-time analytic solution for small analytic initial data. Moreover, for ill-prepared data, we rigorously justify the global-in-time relaxation (Newtonian) limit as the relaxation parameter \(τ\to0\), with an explicit convergence rate of order \(O(\sqrtτ)\).

A recently proposed reaction-diffusion model for the tulip breaking virus (TBV) has been shown to generate striped pigmentation patterns on growing tulip petals. In this paper, we investigate the formation of localized spike patterns in this model in the asymptotic limit of small viral diffusivity. It is known that two distinct bifurcation mechanisms can occur which generate new spikes as the domain half-length $L$ slowly increases: spike self-replication and spike nucleation. Self-replication occurs through a saddle-node bifurcation of the inner spike core problem, whereas nucleation is associated with a fold of the nonlinear outer problem. Using matched asymptotic expansions, we derive critical conditions for these mechanisms and construct phase diagrams that predict which mechanism occurs first as $L$ increases, or whether nucleation is absent. We further combine these results with a Turing instability analysis of the homogeneous steady state to obtain a phase diagram of pattern-forming mechanisms. An interesting finding is that, for the TBV model, the Turing-unstable region lies entirely within the parameter regime where spike nucleation is possible. These results provide further insight into the mechanisms underlying the formation and evolution of pigmentation patterns in virus-infected tulips.

In this paper, we study these families within the framework of blowup analysis developed by C.-S. Lin and his coauthors. We show that the successive bubbling scales for slow decay are determined by the intersections of the ray $H+tq_μ$ with root hyperplanes. At each crossing, rescaling and the face asymptotics identify the limiting profiles as explicit solutions of the corresponding Levi-Toda subsystems. The masses of these successive bubbles, computed using [KLNW24], account for the entire blowup mass. Examples in type $A_2$ demonstrate this identification and exhibit both separated scalar bubbles and a simultaneous full-system bubble.

In the fixed-front region, we combine a one-sided estimate for second angular derivatives with radial and mixed derivative bounds to obtain curvature control without differentiating the Lipschitz directional phase. In the remaining regions, absorptive comparison in the invaded interior, leading-edge barriers and blow-up arguments through the diffusive scale, and Gaussian amplitude estimates combined with parabolic regularity in the exterior yield the required logarithmic-Hessian bounds.

We show that the linearization of the Euler equations around the basic building block plus a small point vortex has an unstable eigenvalue in a space of $3$-fold rotationally symmetric perturbations. We then obtain the scattering matrix, its unitarity and a two-channel optical theorem. The main result is a uniqueness theorem for the inverse problem. Under two geometric conditions on the pair, the scattering amplitude at a single positive energy determines the perturbation completely, and the argument does not distinguish a deformation of the boundary from an obstacle. It follows that no nontrivial perturbation satisfying the same conditions is invisible at any positive energy. On the surface band the corresponding statement is reduced to one explicitly stated question about the exterior Robin problem.

We provide a general ansatz for the paracontrolled approach introduced by Gubinelli, Imkeller, Perkowski for treating singular SPDEs. The ansatz proposed covers a large class of equations. It is described via decorated trees that encode its coefficients and its stochastic data. The main novelty is the recursive definition of the paracontrolled stochastic iterated integrals that involve a well-chosen combinatorial set of words. The paralinearisation is performed via a lift of iterated paraproducts to modelled distributions. The main idea is to integrate localised iterated paraproducts in order to get a global object with a good regularity. We also provide a fixed point argument and the renormalised equation with this ansatz when one uses the preparation map formalism that encompasses the BPHZ renormalisation. The last main result is the convergence of the renormalised stochastic data via the BPHZ renormalisation using an adaptation of the spectral gap approach. One obtains in the end a general solution theory for parabolic singular SPDEs via the paracontrolled approach.

♻ ☆ Mean-field limit of non-exchangeable multi-agent systems over hypergraphs with unbounded rank
Nathalie Ayi, Nastassia Pouradier Duteil, David Poyato
Interacting particle systems are known for their ability to generate large-scale self-organized structures from simple local interaction rules between each agent and its neighbors. In addition to studying their emergent behavior, a main focus of the mathematical community has been concentrated on deriving their large-population limit. In particular, the mean-field limit consists of describing the limit system by its population density in the product space of positions and labels. The strategy to derive such limits is often based on a careful combination of methods ranging from analysis of PDEs and stochastic analysis, to kinetic equations and graph theory. In this article, we focus on a generalization of multi-agent systems that includes higher-order interactions, which has largely captured the attention of the applied community in the last years. In such models, interactions between individuals are no longer assumed to be binary (i.e. between a pair of particles). Instead, individuals are allowed to interact by groups so that a full group jointly generates a non-linear force on any given individual. The underlying graph of connections is then replaced by a hypergraph, which we assume to be dense, but possibly non uniform and of unbounded rank. For the first time in the literature, we show that when the interaction kernels are regular enough, then the mean-field limit is determined by a limiting Vlasov-type equation, where the hypergraph limit is encoded by a so-called UR-hypergraphon (unbounded-rank hypergraphon), and where the resulting mean-field force admits infinitely-many orders of interactions.

Moreover, we prove asymptotic completeness of the wave operators intertwining Hardy operators with and without external short-range perturbations. We also show the nonexistence of the considered wave operators when the Hardy or external potentials are long-range. We arrive at these results using three different approaches. The first approach uses an abstract semigroup framework for asymptotic completeness of wave operators for Fourier multipliers with short-range potentials. The second approach uses Kato smoothness theory. In the third approach, we develop and apply new propagation estimates for Hardy operators with and without perturbations.

We develop a method for studying centralizers of generic elements in some large Polish groups. This approach enables us to answer the question that motivated this work : we prove that a generic isometry of the Urysohn space (or the Urysohn sphere) embeds in a flow. We also obtain information on the centralizer of a generic isometry; we show that it contains an infinite-dimensional torus and that torsion elements are dense in it. To illustrate the flexibility of our method, we apply it to two other Polish groups. The first is the group of measure-preserving automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we recover results of King and of de la Rue and de Sam Lazaro. Finally we apply our technique to the group of nonsingular automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we deduce that a generic nonsingular automorphism embeds in a flow, answering a question of Danilenko and Silva.

Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and let $\mathbb Z$ act by bilateral shifts. We prove that the quotient $\mathbb S(\mathcal H)/\mathbb Z$ of the unit sphere, equipped with its quotient metric, has infinite Hilbert distortion. Consequently, $\mathcal H/\mathbb Z$ does not admit a bilipschitz embedding into Hilbert space, answering a question of Cahill, Iverson, and Mixon. The proof first embeds every flat torus $\mathbb R^n/L$, after rescaling, into the quotient $\mathbb S\big(\ell^2(\mathbb Z^n)\big)/\mathbb Z^n$ with distortion arbitrarily close to $1$, where $\mathbb Z^n$ acts by translations. ☆ Bounded symbols and one-component geometry

We prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on a Hardy model space admits a bounded symbol if and only if its defining inner function is one-component, meaning that it has a connected sublevel set at some level in $(0,1)$. This resolves the bounded symbol conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi and Timotin and, through known equivalences, the embedding and weak factorization conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin. A uniform bound $R$ for the ratio of least bounded symbol norm to operator norm on the rank-one family associated with point evaluation in the disk already forces this geometry. The corresponding bound for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators is at most $CR\log(e+R)$, where $C$ is absolute, and the logarithmic factor is optimal. In a nonzero de Branges space, the same geometric condition characterizes when every sufficiently small equivalent change of norm preserving the de Branges structure is represented exactly by reweighting the original integral with a positive density bounded above and away from zero. This characterization remains valid when the norm changes are restricted to discrete sampling norms. Outside the one-component class, every model space admits self-adjoint trace class truncated Toeplitz operators without bounded symbols, with arbitrarily small norm and singular values satisfying any prescribed positive upper bounds.

☆ Optimal weighted sampling of positive and normal operator orbits
Jian Wu
We study weighted sampling of operator orbit frames in infinite dimensional separable Hilbert spaces \(H\), keeping the operator and generating vectors fixed. Let $N_μ(R)$ count the sampling times in $[0,R]$. For a single orbit of a positive operator, let $m_A(R)$ count the eigenvalues in $(0,e^{-1/R}]$. Every real sampling design that preserves the frame property must satisfy the lower bound $N_μ(R)\ge m_A(R)-O_μ(1)$. Conversely, for every $η>0$, we construct an integer sampling design that preserves the frame property and satisfies $N_μ(R)\le(1+η)m_A(R)+O_η(1)$. Thus the coefficient $1$ is optimal. Under additional spectral conditions, we attain $N_μ(R)=m_A(R)+O(1)$ and characterize the weights that preserve the frame property on the constructed sets. For finitely or countably many orbits of a positive operator, let $P_j$, $j\ge1$, be the spectral projection corresponding to $2^{-j-1}<-\logλ\le2^{-j}$ and define $K_A(R)=\#\{j\ge1:2^j\le R,\ P_j\ne0\}$. Every real sampling design that preserves the frame property satisfies $N_μ(R)\ge c_μK_A(R)-C_μ$ for $R\ge2$, with constants $c_μ>0$ and $C_μ\ge0$. Conversely, we construct an integer sampling design that preserves the frame property and satisfies $N_μ(R)\le L K_A(R)+L$ for $R\ge2$, where $L$ depends only on the bounds of the given orbit frame. For normal operators of norm one, we prove that the smallest frame condition number is attained among integer sampling designs that preserve the frame property and satisfy a prescribed counting bound, whenever this class is nonempty. Finally, we construct one normal operator with two families of generating vectors for which the optimal growth orders of $N_μ(R)$ are $\log R$ and $R$, respectively, for both real and integer sampling.

We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fréchet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.

For $k=4$, however, the ordinary rectifiability conclusion can fail even for norms arbitrarily close to Euclidean: we construct norms on $\mathbb R^3$ with smooth positively curved unit spheres arbitrarily $C^\infty$-close to the Euclidean sphere, together with four-point sets whose ordinary $4$-medial axes contain nondegenerate line segments.

The argument realizes arbitrary matrix amplifications of a shifted Toeplitz symbol inside rectangular corners of the original multiplier. It also applies to some locally finite trees of unbounded degree. Consequently, the completely bounded radial multiplier theorem of González-Pérez, Parcet, Pérez García and Wang has no general counterpart with ordinary norms. We also determine the optimal order of the comparison constant for positive definite even symbols. For each $1 < p < \infty$ with $p \neq 2$, we construct radial symbols on finitely generated nonabelian free groups, supported in the ball of radius $N$, whose completely bounded Herz--Schur norms remain bounded as $N \to \infty$, whereas their ordinary Fourier multiplier norms grow at least like $N^{|1-\frac{2}{p}|}$. For each fixed $0 < \vartheta < π$, we also determine the exact order $t^{-|1-\frac{2}{p}|}$ of both the ordinary and completely bounded Fourier multiplier norms of the damped radial phases $s \mapsto \mathrm{e}^{(-t+\mathrm{i}\vartheta)|s|}$ as $t \to 0$. Finally, we compute the local amenability modulus of free balls, we bound the Fourier--Schur ratio of free balls from above and below in terms of this modulus, and we show that its restriction to radial symbols grows polynomially in the radius.

We study conditions that imply finite-dimensionality of metrizable or Frechet-Urysohn linear subspaces of topological vector spaces (TVS). We consider the classes $\mathscr{D}_M$ and $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ of TVS: a space $L$ belongs to $\mathscr{D}_M$ (respectively, $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$) if every metrizable (respectively, Frechet-Urysohn) linear subspace of $L$ is finite-dimensional. Although the classes of metrizable spaces and of Frechet-Urysohn spaces differ substantially, the classes $\mathscr{D}_M$ and $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ are much closer to each other: in the Hrusak-Ramos-Garcia model, in which Malykhin's problem is solved, $\mathscr{D}_M=\mathscr{D}_{FU}$, whereas under MA+not CH, as shown in the paper, $\mathscr{D}_M\neq\mathscr{D}_{FU}$. For a locally convex space (LCS) $L$ we denote by $L_w$ the space $L$ with its weak topology and by $L'_{w^*}$ the dual space with the weak$^*$ topology. This paper investigates which LCS $L$ have the property that $L_w$ and $L'_{w^*}$ belong to $\mathscr{D}_M$ or $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$. Although the classes are close, different methods are used to study them: topological-algebraic ones for $\mathscr{D}_M$ (a criterion is obtained) and methods of measure theory and probability for $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ (a sufficient condition is obtained). We prove that if an LCS $L$ admits a continuous norm, then $L_w\in\mathscr{D}_{FU}$; in particular, if $L$ admits a continuous norm and $L_w$ is Frechet-Urysohn, then $L$ is finite-dimensional. If the topology of an LCS $L$ is coarser than the topology induced by some complete norm on $L$ (for example, if $L$ is Banach), then $L'_{w^*}\in\mathscr{D}_{FU}$; completeness of the norm is essential here. The methods also apply to spaces of real-analytic functions and to the space of polynomials with the topology of pointwise convergence: these also belong to $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$.

A central problem in harmonic analysis is to understand how frequency resolution constrains stability under nonlinear changes of coordinates. Motivated by Mallat's wavelet scattering theory, we establish a sharp resolution--robustness principle for nonlinear representations built from two-dimensional wave-packet systems, showing that the transverse geometry of the frequency channels determines the critical Sobolev regularity. Whenever the channels are thinner than in the wavelet regime, arbitrarily small smooth deformations can move high-frequency mass between adjacent channels, producing instability already at the level of the linear filter bank and the first scattering layer. We match this obstruction with scale-sharp commutator estimates propagated through the full scattering cascade, obtaining Lipschitz stability at the critical regularity threshold. Together, the results provide the first intrinsic deformation-stability theory for non-wavelet Euclidean scattering transforms and identify a microlocal transport mechanism governing robustness across nonlinear multiscale representations.

A key ingredient is a variable-coefficient elliptic theory developed using quasiconformal mappings and Schauder estimates in certain scale-invariant Hölder spaces. We are unaware of any previous nonperturbative class of time-dependent solutions to the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Euler equations for which global well-posedness has been established. Finally, for some signed global solutions, we show a dichotomy between density homogenization and averaged relaxation in infinite time.

In 1877 Gröbli discovered that three point vortices in the plane can move self-similarly, forming a triangle that rotates while either expanding indefinitely or collapsing in finite time. We study the viscous counterpart of these configurations, namely the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes evolution starting from three point vortices arranged in a Gröbli triangle. As an application of the long-time result in the expanding case, we obtain a vanishing viscosity realization of the vortex burst, a nonuniqueness mechanism for point vortices in which a single vortex splits into an expanding Gröbli triangle.

We establish nonlinear inviscid damping of the near-Couette flows in a finite channel, with vorticity perturbations vanishing to infinite order at the boundary. To study the boundary effect, we decompose the vorticity into dyadic layers whose supports expand toward the boundary, and use an inductive Newton scheme to track nonlinear interactions across layers. Finally, precise elliptic estimates are established to quantify the velocity generated by different layers.

We study the saturation property on smooth compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary. Our approach relies on the existence of an isometric embedding of the manifold into $\mathbb{R}^n$ due to Nash. As an application, we obtain global approximate controllability in arbitrarily small time for the bilinear Schrödinger equation on any connected compact Riemannian manifold, with finitely many potentials.

Their phase saturation contains the representative algebra and is therefore dense in $L^2$. We extend this construction to normal homogeneous quotients using finite generation of the algebra of highest-weight functions. Global controllability follows by combining the phase-to-gradient transport argument of [8] with the gradient generation theorem of [23] and Moser's transport of positive densities.

We design a neural operator for the two-dimensional Boussinesq system with anisotropic dissipation on the periodic box, guided by a rigorous analysis of its long-time behavior. The operator maps a small perturbation of hydrostatic equilibrium, of amplitude $\varepsilon$, to the vorticity at a late time. We prove that the flow relaxes to a stratified shear flow, with the horizontally averaged vorticity staying within $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of its initial value $\barω_0$ and the oscillation about it of order $\varepsilon$. Accordingly, the network outputs $\barω_0$ plus these two parts, each scaled to its size, which grows as $\varepsilon^2$ and $\varepsilon$, respectively. Without this guidance the training either does not converge or misses the $\varepsilon^2$ growth. With it, one network reproduces, sample by sample on $2\times10^3$ test runs over a factor of $23$ in amplitude, the quantity bounded by the theorem to a median error of $2.2$ percent. Being fast and differentiable with respect to the initial data, the network is also used to search the space of initial data, and with every candidate checked by the solver the search finds initial data for which this quantity is $4.4$ times the largest value among the test runs, raising the lower bound for the constant of the theorem by that factor.

We prove that, for the adiabatic exponent $γ\in(1,2]$, the solution to the NSFK system converges uniformly in space, as time tends to infinity, to a composite wave consisting of a rarefaction wave, a viscous contact wave, and a viscous-dispersive shock with a time-dependent shift, provided that the initial perturbation and the strengths of the contact wave and the shock are sufficiently small. In particular, we do not impose any smallness condition on the strength of the rarefaction wave. Because of the capillarity, the shock is viscous-dispersive and its profile equation is of third order. We treat the shock by the method of $a$-contraction with shifts introduced by Kang and Vasseur. This is the first result on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous-dispersive shock, and of a generic Riemann solution, for the NSFK system.

This ``paired comparison'' simplification yields immediate nonlinear extensions: the disk minimizes the clamped quotient $\|Δu\|_q/\|u\|_p$ among bounded open sets of prescribed area, for every $1\le p,q\le\infty$. In higher dimensions, we prove ball minimality for $p=\infty$ and conjecture minimality for all $p,q$ within the compact embedding range. In dimensions one and two, the paired comparison holds for all $1\le p\le\infty$, and it holds in every dimension for $p=\infty$. The inequalities are sharp and equality cases are characterized. In dimensions $n \geq 3$, paired comparison can fail for every finite $p$ although it remains valid for $p\ge(3n-1)/4$ in the special case of bang-bang sources with mean zero. The mean-zero source assumption is crucial when $p<\infty$. Without it, paired comparison can fail even for bang-bang sources. For sources of arbitrary mean in one dimension, however, the $L^\infty$ paired comparison still holds and so does a comparison for $L^p$ norms of the derivative when $1\le p\le3$.

The nonlinear analysis demonstrates that the spinorial structures remain essential on the black-hole background. We show that the viscous stationary solution is uniformly approximated by the superposition of the limiting stationary solution and a boundary-layer profile. Here, the boundary layer appears only for the density and velocity, whereas no boundary-layer appears for the temperature. Moreover, for any $α\in (0,1)$, the approximation error is of order $O(μ^α)$.

On a bounded interval with Neumann boundary conditions, we construct smooth, time-independent transmission and recovery rates satisfying \(β(x)>γ(x)>0\), together with diffusion coefficients \(d_I>d_S>0\), such that periodic solutions coexist with the unique endemic equilibrium for every prescribed positive total population. Thus, pointwise dominance of transmission over recovery does not ensure convergence to equilibrium. Our approach combines an inverse construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium with a coefficient path that preserves both the equilibrium and the pointwise inequalities. A change in the number of unstable eigenvalues along this path yields small-amplitude periodic solutions through a center-manifold reduction and a generalized Hopf bifurcation argument. The proof uses an AI-assisted construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium under the pointwise condition $β>γ>0$.

Nonetheless, the global regularity problem remains completely open. The sharpest known regularity criteria in terms of the circulation are slightly subcritical, namely $|Γ|\lesssim(\log r^{-1})^{-k}$ near the symmetry axis; Lei and Zhang proved regularity for $k=2$, and Wei later lowered the exponent to $k=3/2$. In this note, we strengthen the criterion further to $k=5/4$. The argument follows the usual route of energy estimates for the quantities $ω^r/r$ and $ω^θ/r$, but now with a sharper bound on the vortex stretching term in the equation for $ω^r/r$, in which the loss is proportional only to the square root of the number of scales between the inner vortex core and the far field.

In this paper we introduce a compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for the Euler equations of compressible gas dynamics, which preserves a minimum entropy principle similar to that introduced by Tadmor for entropy solution of the Euler equations [4]. Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.

We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.

☆ Local Optimality of the d-cube for Laplacian Eigenvalues

For each $d \ge 2$ we prove that the unit $d$-cube $\square_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is, on the class $\mathcal{P}$ of convex polytopes combinatorially equivalent to a $d$-cube, (i) a strict local minimizer of the scale-invariant isoperimetric ratio $I(Ω) = \tfrac{P(Ω)^d}{|Ω|^{d-1}}$, with $P$ the perimeter, (ii) a strict local minimizer of the volume-normalized first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\barλ(Ω) = |Ω|^{2/d}λ_1(Ω)$, and (iii) a strict local maximizer of the volume-normalized first Neumann eigenvalue $\barμ(Ω) = |Ω|^{2/d}μ_1(Ω)$. The method is a shape-derivative Hessian analysis adapted to the hyperoctahedral symmetry of the cube. In symmetry-adapted coordinates on the parameter space --- the decomposition into irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group --- each Hessian is block-diagonal, with four scalar eigenvalues, which we give in closed form in $π$, rational coefficients, and a few universal series-constants. The first Neumann eigenvalue is not differentiable at $\square_d$, since its lowest cluster splits under perturbation. The Neumann case therefore works with a smooth auxiliary functional, whose Hessian is computed by second-order perturbation theory of the cluster; the coupling to modes outside the cluster enters at the same order. Finally, we show that extremality of $I$, $\barλ$, and $\barμ$ does not hold in high dimensions for a particular multilinear perturbation that leaves $\mathcal{P}$ by breaking convexity. All results are local; we discuss why a global statement, available for quadrilaterals (Endo and Osting, 2026), appears out of reach for $d \ge 3$.

In other words, the Serrin exponent of the sum is the smallest of the Serrin exponents $N/κ_i$ of the single operators, that is, the one of the operator whose fundamental solution decays fastest. No structural assumption relating the different operators is needed. The endpoint $q=\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ is left open. The local order $s_i=1$ is treated together with the nonlocal orders, and all the arguments are carried out in the weak setting.

☆ Source integrability and the frontier $α=\tfrac12$ in time-fractional diffusion
Edison A. Vásquez-Martínez, Mauricio A. Londoño-Arboleda
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, let $α\in(0,1)$, and let $\partial_{t}^α$ denote the Caputo derivative. For $\partial_{t}^αu-\nabla\cdot\bigl(A(x)\nabla u\bigr)=f$ with homogeneous Dirichlet condition and initial datum $g\in L^{2}(Ω)$, we identify which of the thresholds appearing in the energy method belong to the method and which to the equation. We compare $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ and $f\in L^{r}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ with $r>2/α$; in the subdiffusive range the second implies the first and not conversely. Existence is not at issue and we claim none of it: it is known, for both hypotheses and under weaker ones, from the work of Zacher. What we determine is the exact set of exponents each route admits and what the exponents left outside it cost. Under the weaker hypothesis the construction below reaches $α\in(\frac12,1)$, under the stronger one every $α\in(0,1)$, and in both cases the solution lies in $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$, by the mode representation and not by the energy route, which yields no such bound under the weaker hypothesis. The restriction $α>\frac12$ comes from the compactness criterion, whose admissible exponents form $[1,2α)$; the exponent $r>2/α$ is exactly what the Grönwall step consumes. A concentrating family shows that nothing weaker suffices along that route, and the mode representation lowers the requirement to $1/α$. The frontier $α=\frac12$ belongs to the equation: for every $α\in(0,\frac12]$ there is $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ whose weak solution leaves $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$. Uniqueness and Hadamard well-posedness follow.

☆ Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff

We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.

Next, assuming $M$ has bounded geometry (not necessarily compact), and given critical points with $\varepsilon^{-1}\mathcal{Y}_{\varepsilon}(\nabla_{\varepsilon}, Φ_{\varepsilon})$ uniformly bounded, we show that as $\varepsilon\to 0$, the energy measures $\varepsilon^{-1}e_{\varepsilon}(\nabla_{\varepsilon}, Φ_{\varepsilon}) \mathrm{vol}_{g}$ converge subsequentially to \[ |h|^2 \mathrm{vol}_g + \sum_{x \in S}Θ(x)δ_{x}, \] where $h$ is an $L^2$ harmonic $1$-form, $S$ a finite set and each $Θ(x)$ equals the energy of a finite collection of $\mathcal{Y}_{1}$-critical points on $\mathbb{R}^3$. As a byproduct of our results, we deduce the existence of non-trivial $\mathcal{Y}_{1}$-critical points over $\mathbb{R}^3$ for any $λ>0$.

One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are repulsive at short range and attractive at long range are useful simplified models that describe biological aggregation. In the current work we employ new techniques to treat compactly supported solutions in the case where the potential is $C^1$ and satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions although it is not necessarily semiconvex, as required in previous work. Central to this approach are uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system, which requires the potential be only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. In the semiconvex case, these bounds also yield convergence of time-shifted trajectories to an eternal solution. The tradeoff, just as in the case of repulsive Euler-Poisson, is that we cannot claim that the emerging solutions for non-semiconvex potentials are sticky.

Fixed commutators without sound-speed weights exhibit a first-order null structure, while subtraction of explicit approximate solutions produces damping that cancels the leading antidamping bulk terms in the energy identity. An explicit analysis of the initial-slice ODEs identifies fractional powers and logarithmic terms at zero sound speed. The logarithmic coefficients couple vorticity to tangential variation of the initial data, revealing an obstruction to higher spatial regularity even when the powers of the sound speed have integer exponents. This analysis determines the finite approximation order used to close the energy and geometric estimates in the stated range. These ingredients provide the geometric and energy framework for the forthcoming second paper of this series, which will use finite evolving profiles to treat the full range $γ\in(1,\frac53]$.

In this paper, we show that the linear operator $\partial^2_{xx} - B$ is not necessarily a sectorial operator in any version of the uniformly local Lebesgue space, due to the possible non-density of its domain. Then, we use the theory of parabolic abstract evolution equations to set a well-posed Cauchy problem, even in the weak version of the uniformly local space. In particular, we believe that this paper offers a new perspective on the comparison between both versions of the uniformly local spaces and also provides a new natural example of differential operators with non-dense domain.

We work in spatial dimensions $d \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ with $d < 4H$, where $H \in (\frac{1}{2}, 1)$ is the Hurst parameter of the noise, and apply Malliavin calculus to investigate the existence of a density for the solution $u$. In particular, we show that $u$ admits a jointly continuous modification and construct a localizing sequence through which we prove that its Malliavin derivative exists locally, and that its law is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$, thereby establishing that a density exists. We obtain the result for the whole range of dimensions and Hurst parameters in which the mild solution is known to exist. The analysis rests on three new estimates. The first bounds the expectation of the $p$-th power ($p \geq 2$) of the $L^{\infty}(D)$-norm of the stochastic integral appearing in the mild formulation. The other two concern the integral involving the operator associated with the kernel that appears in the integral representation of the fractional noise: an upper estimate and, more importantly, a lower estimate on short time intervals, which yields the nondegeneracy of the Malliavin derivative.

The nonlinearity has critical exponential growth in the sense of the Trudinger-Moser inequality. Using variational methods, the associated Pohožaev manifold, and suitable Moser-type estimates, we establish the existence of a normalized solution of mountain-pass type with associated non zero Lagrange multiplier. Under an additional monotonicity assumption on the nonlinearity, we further show that the obtained solution is a normalized ground state. We also establish the regularity properties required for the proof of the corresponding Pohožaev identity.
♻ ☆ A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations

We give new proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the Monge-Ampère equation and the constant quadratic Hessian equation, based on the two-point maximum principle. The arguments require only one differentiation of the equation. For the Monge-Ampère equation, the inhomogeneous term is assumed to be positive and continuously differentiable. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.
♻ ☆ A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang
In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

♻ ☆ Stability of the Shape for Circular Vortex Filaments under Non-Symmetric Perturbations
Masashi Aiki, Mitsuo Higaki
We establish the nonlinear orbital stability of circular vortex filaments governed by the Localized Induction Equation (LIE) under non-symmetric perturbations, within the framework of [Tani-Nishiyama, 1997]. This result extends the first author's recent work [Aiki, 2025] by removing symmetry assumptions on perturbations. While the circular filaments are known to be Lyapunov unstable due to linear growth of the translational mode, we prove that their shape remains globally stable modulo spatial translations and rotations about the symmetry axis. The crucial ingredient is a geometric stability estimate derived from the conservation of vector fluid impulse, which constrains the low-frequency modulations that are not covered by the relative energy. Finally, we relate the fluid impulse to an isoperimetric inequality, yielding a geometric constraint for closed filaments.

♻ ☆ Mixed Third-Order Flux Laws for Dual Cascade in the Stochastic SQG Equation
Rongchang Liu, Kening Lu, Zexin Wang
We study dual-cascade flux laws for the stochastic forced--dissipative surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equation on a large periodic box. For statistically stationary solutions, under a weak anomalous dissipation assumption, we derive rigorous mixed third-order structure-function laws for the dual cascade: a Yaglom-type law for the direct cascade of surface potential energy (SPE) and a mixed flux law for the inverse cascade of the Hamiltonian. We further establish complementary scaling laws: a cubic small-scale law for the Hamiltonian structure function and a large-scale vanishing law for the SPE structure function. In particular, both Hamiltonian laws appear to be new for SQG even as an explicit third-order structure-function relation. We also prove Onsager-type obstruction results showing that sufficiently regular stationary families cannot sustain the corresponding non-zero fluxes: $B^s_{3,\infty}$-regularity above the Onsager threshold $1/3$ rules out the direct SPE flux, while sufficient low-frequency Besov regularity rules out the inverse Hamiltonian flux. These results provide a rigorous formulation of the SQG dual-cascade phenomenology in a stochastic stationary setting.
♻ ☆ Lyapunov Unstable Motion Bifurcating from a Circular Vortex Filament
Masashi Aiki, Mitsuo Higaki
This paper investigates the dynamics of closed vortex filaments in $\R^3$ governed by the Localized Induction Equation. Recently, Aiki and Higaki (2026) established the nonlinear orbital stability of circular vortex filaments under asymmetric perturbations, while identifying Lyapunov instability due to the linear growth of translation modes. Motivated by this result, we prove the existence of a family of closed solutions, which we call axial screw motions, that bifurcate from a circular filament. These solutions remain uniformly close to the orbit of the circle, but drift secularly away from the reference motion because their translation speed along the symmetry axis differs from that of the circular filament. In particular, they provide explicit non-trivial perturbations that satisfy orbital-stability estimates while failing Lyapunov stability, thereby realizing the gap between orbital stability and Lyapunov stability near the circular filament.

We derive long-time asymptotic estimates for small solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KPII) equation using inverse scattering theory, contour deformation, and stationary phase analysis. Under a suitable smallness condition and explicit regularity and decay assumptions on the initial data, the estimates hold uniformly in regimes separated from the transition region, without imposing nonphysical conditions on the scattering data. We establish reduced representation formulas for the nonlinear contributions in terms of ABF (Ablowitz--Bar Yaacov--Fokas) Cauchy integrals with controlled remainders. Their analysis yields $o_ε(t^{-19/20+ε})$ and $o_ε(t^{-11/12+ε})$ estimates in the positive and negative regimes, respectively, while stationary phase analysis determines the asymptotics of the linear contribution.

Amer. Math. Soc. 141:1979-1993, 2013) that the domain must be distant from the axis of symmetry. ♻ ☆ The Shubin--Vakilian--Wolff Uncertainty Principle at Half Density
Ming Wang, Yunlei Wang
Shubin, Vakilian, and Wolff proved a Fourier uncertainty principle for sets of sufficiently small local density at the reciprocal scale and asked whether every density below one is admissible. We answer this question negatively in dimension one by constructing sequences of pairs of $1/2$-density thin sets and unit vectors whose total position and Fourier mass outside these sets tends to zero. This obstruction persists for every scaled reciprocal profile $ρ_κ(x)=\min\{1,κ/|x|\}$, $κ>0$. On the other hand, for $0<κ\le1$, the uncertainty estimate holds whenever the density $$ \varepsilon<\frac{1}{2(1+32κ)}. $$ Thus the critical density tends to $1/2$ as $κ\downarrow 0$. The obstruction uses odd Gaussian packets to transfer norm bounds from a free-group model. The positive estimate uses a Fourier-complementary anti-Wick operator and quadratic straightening of the reciprocal geometry.

♻ ☆ Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
Andrey Morgulis, Karrar Malal
We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization, and something like blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.

☆ Unitary similarity for dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices
Cailing Yao, Bingzhe Hou, Xiaoqi Feng
We study unitary similarity of dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices. First, we characterize unitary similarity in terms of the existence of a skew-Hermitian solution to a Sylvester-type matrix equation. For $2\times2$ dual complex matrices, we obtain a complete three-trace criterion when the standard part is nonnormal and analyze the limitations of trace-word criteria when the standard part is normal. We then prove, for every $n\geq1$, that two $n\times n$ dual quaternion matrices are unitarily similar if and only if their dual complex adjoint matrices are unitarily similar, and we extend this result to finite families. As a scalar consequence, we derive a finite Trace-word criterion when the standard part is nonreal and exhibit its failure when the standard part is real.

Area-preserving parameterization of triangular meshes is an essential task in geometry processing, yet an exactly area-preserving simplicial mapping may not exist in general. In this paper, we study area preservation of simplicial mappings in the limit of mesh refinement by establishing the $Γ$-convergence of the discrete stretch energy, a functional that measures their area distortion. We first introduce its limit functional, the relaxed stretch energy on surface homeomorphisms, defined through the pushforward of the area measure, and show that it is the relaxation of the stretch energy of diffeomorphisms with respect to uniform convergence. Then, to compare simplicial mappings with homeomorphisms, we construct a geometric lift that requires no shape-regularity assumption on the image mesh. Finally, we establish the $Γ$-convergence and show that the minimal discrete energies converge to the continuum minimum. Moreover, any homeomorphism arising as a limit of lifted discrete local minimizers in fixed-radius balls is area-preserving.
