We study finite products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space over the complex plane. If every symbol has the form $f+\overline g$, where $f$ and $g$ are entire functions of exponential type, we prove that a finite product vanishes if and only if one symbol vanishes identically. It suffices to test the product on reproducing kernels. The proof represents the product by a two-variable entire function and transforms the equation for a left factor by $\exp(-\partial_z\partial_w)$. A Fock norm identity then permits cancellation of each nonzero factor.

We investigate the well-posedness and long-time behavior of a general continuum neural field model with Gaussian noise on possibly unbounded domains. In particular, we give conditions for the existence of invariant probability measures by restricting the solution flow to an invariant subspace with a nonlocal metric. Under the assumption of a sufficiently large decay parameter relative to the noise intensity, the norm of the connectivity kernel operator, and the Lipschitz regularity of the activation function, we establish exponential ergodicity and exponential mixing of the associated Markovian Feller semigroup and the uniqueness of the invariant measure.

In the Gaussian case, we characterize those functions that arise from covariance operators in terms of $γ$-radonifying operators. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. ♻ ☆ A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang
In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

♻ ☆ Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions and Fujii-Seo Determinants in Hilbert spaces
Per Åhag, Rafał Czyż, Antti Perälä, Jani Virtanen
A maximal plurisubharmonic function on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space can have an injective, noncompact Levi operator at every point. This raises the question of what replaces the finite-dimensional determinant criterion for maximality. We prove that a twice continuously differentiable plurisubharmonic function is maximal if its Levi operator is compact at every point, without any boundedness assumption on the function. Using the normalized determinants of Fujii and Seo, we also characterize local maximality by the condition that the infimum of the spectrum of the Levi operator is zero. The same condition characterizes maximality when the function is bounded on the closure of every bounded open set whose closure lies in the domain. The compactness result follows from a more general spectral criterion. Its proof combines a bounded transformation with the smooth variational principle of Borwein and Preiss to establish comparison on bounded open sets whose closures need not be compact.
♻ ☆ A survey of sampling discretization of integral and uniform norms
F. Dai, E. Kosov, V. Temlyakov
This paper surveys recent developments in the sampling discretization of integral and uniform norms for functions in general finite-dimensional spaces. These results generalize the classical Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities for trigonometric and algebraic polynomials, which play a crucial role in Fourier analysis, interpolation, and approximation theory. We focus on the problem in the broad context of finite-dimensional subspaces, where norms defined by general probability measures are approximated by their discrete counterparts. The primary emphasis is on results closely related to the authors' recent research. A key objective is to highlight the main ideas and techniques that form the foundation of the proofs in this area. This survey serves as a complement to three recently published survey papers on sampling discretization \cite{DPTT, KKLT, LMT}.
♻ ☆ Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups

We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert-Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.

☆ Local well-posedness of wave kinetic equations associated with water waves
Yu Deng, Alexandru D. Ionescu, Fabio Pusateri
We prove two conceptually different local well-posedness results for wave kinetic equations associated with water-wave systems. For pure gravity waves with 2D interfaces, we establish a classical well-posedness theory in weighted Sobolev spaces: regularity is propagated, and solutions depend continuously on the initial data in the same topology. For gravity-capillary waves with one-dimensional interfaces, the situation is fundamentally different. We prove well-posedness in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces (in the sense of existence, uniqueness, and continuity in a weaker topology), but we also show that, in general, any additional regularity of the initial data is instantly lost. Moreover, continuity in time and continuous dependence on the initial data fail in the weighted $L^\infty$ norm, even for smooth compactly supported initial data. This instability is caused by degenerate three-wave resonances, which produce singular collision rates and arbitrarily short relaxation time scales. The distinction between the two theories reflects a fundamental difference in their resonant geometry.

In this paper, we establish the asymptotic local optimality of the BCC lattice under small periodic perturbations, extending its known stability beyond the class of lattice configurations. Our approach connects the discrete geometry of Voronoi tessellations with a continuum variational problem, showing that the rescaled quadratic quantization energies converge to a continuum functional describing locally deformed BCC lattices. A central ingredient is a geometric and algebraic framework that combines the stability of the BCC Voronoi structure, a discrete calculus on its adjacency graph and an analysis of the lattice symmetries via representation theory, allowing us to establish the positivity of the second variation at the BCC configuration and thereby prove the local minimality of the BCC lattice for the limiting energy.

All statements concern the instantaneous fixed-mode linearization. The singularity is a property of the phase coupling, not of the thin geometry.

For the massless Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we establish a Landis-type estimate showing that the vanishing order of any nontrivial bounded solution of $( \mathcal{D}_n + \mathbb{V} ) \varphi = 0$ satisfies a lower bound of order $\exp(-κR^{2} (\log R)^{2})$ as $|x|=R\to \infty$; the quadratic growth in the exponent is sharp, in view of previous known results. Our proof follows a Bourgain--Kenig type approach based on a Carleman inequality for Dirac operators which relies on a local Hölder regularity result, which we also prove. In two dimension, we obtain improved quantitative estimates under symmetry assumptions on the potential $\mathbb{V}$ and for real-valued solutions. Finally, we also derive qualitative Landis-type results for Dirac equations with decaying potentials, including critical decay rates.

♻ ☆ A mass-type invariant for smooth metric measure spaces and its relation with the fractional Yamabe problem
Sergio Almaraz, Levi Lopes de Lima, Shaodong Wang
On asymptotically Schwarzschild smooth metric measure spaces modeled on the Euclidean half-space, we define a new mass-type invariant analogous to the ADM mass of an asymptotically flat manifold. We prove that this invariant is independent of the choice of admissible asymptotic coordinates. We further show that it fits into a very general framework for mass-type invariants and we also isolate static equations for smooth metric measure spaces under natural boundary conditions. For smooth metric measure spaces obtained through a generalized stereographic projection using the Green's function associated with the fractional Yamabe problem, we identify the mass with the constant term in the asymptotic expansion of the Green's function. This identification gives a geometric interpretation of the constant appearing in the fractional Yamabe problem and recasts its conjectured positivity as a positive-mass-type question.

♻ ☆ A deterministic particle approximation for a fourth-order equation
Charles Elbar, Alejandro Fernández-Jiménez
We provide a deterministic particle approximation to a fourth order equation with applications in cell-cell adhesion. In order to do that, first we show that the equation can be asymptotically obtained as a limit from a class of well-posed nonlocal partial differential equations. These latter have the advantage that the particles' empirical measure naturally satisfies the equation. Afterwards, we obtain stability of the 2-Wasserstein gradient flow of this family of nonlocal equations that we use in order to recover a deterministic particle approximation of the fourth order equation. Up to our knowledge, in this manuscript we derive the first deterministic particle approximation for a fourth-order partial differential equation. Finally, we give some numerical simulations of the model at the particles level.

We investigate the $Γ$-convergence of Ambrosio-Tortorelli type-functionals for circle valued functions, in the case of volume terms with linear growth. We show the emergence of a non-local $Γ$-limit, which is due to the topological structure of the target space, and discuss compactness of minimal liftings. Our results extend the analysis of a previous work on the quadratic case. Applications to the area functional are given.

♻ ☆ Global Sobolev Convergence of Howard Iteration for Finite-Horizon Controlled Diffusions
Linyu Miao
We study Howard policy iteration for finite-horizon stochastic control problems in which the control enters the diffusion coefficient. Each iteration selects a policy by maximizing the Hamiltonian and evaluates it through a linear parabolic equation. Since the improvement depends on the Hessian, even smooth data can produce discontinuous evaluation coefficients. We prove global convergence in the full parabolic Sobolev space under assumptions that allow this loss of regularity. In one space dimension, bounded measurable coefficients and uniform ellipticity suffice, without a large discount, a short horizon, small diffusion variation, or regularity assumptions on the improving policies. Multidimensional extensions hold under structural conditions on the diffusion matrix. The proof combines monotonicity with a parabolic growth estimate to show that the Bellman residual vanishes in measure. Uniform higher integrability then yields strong convergence of the values, gradients, Hessians, and time derivatives, and constructs the unique strong solution. We also establish residual error bounds, extend the argument to entropy regularization and zero-temperature limits, and obtain quadratic convergence for special one-dimensional models.
♻ ☆ On some connections between Kobayashi geometry and pluripotential theory
Gautam Bharali, Rumpa Masanta
In this paper, we explore some connections between Kobayashi geometry and the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Ampère equation. Among the results we obtain through these connections are: $(i)$~a theorem on the continuous extension up to $\partial{D}$ of a proper holomorphic map $F: D\longrightarrow Ω$ between domains with $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}(D) < \dim_{\mathbb{C}}(Ω)$, and $(ii)$~a result that establishes the existence of bounded domains with ``nice'' boundary geometry on which Hölder regularity of the solutions to the complex Monge--Ampère equation fails. The first, a result in Kobayashi geometry, relies upon an auxiliary construction that involves solving the complex Monge--Ampère equation with Hölder estimates. The second result relies crucially on a bound for the Kobayashi metric.

We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A\nabla)+\B\cdot\nabla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{\textup{loc}}(Ω)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, using AI, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-Δ+\B\cdot\nabla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.

♻ ☆ A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
Thuyen Dang, Yuliya Gorb, Silvia Jiménez Bolaños
We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by Tartar's vision of a \emph{point-free} theory, we derive explicit norm resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting technique and solve a generalized Sylvester equation that controls the commutator between the differential structure and the highly oscillatory material properties. This abstract perspective unifies stationary, non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions between these media--and their respective convergence rates--are entirely captured by the behavior of the spectral measures of the microscopic and macroscopic derivative operators near zero frequency.

♻ ☆ Narrow escape problems beyond spherical holes: slits and tubes

The narrow escape problem consists in characterizing the exit event of a Brownian motion trapped inside a domain with reflecting boundary and small absorbing holes. Using recent advances in the quasi-stationary distribution approach, we first give an explicit set of hypotheses that allows one to derive the asymptotics of the exit time and of the exit hole distribution. We then apply it in dimension three to several hole shapes: spherical holes, thin spheroidal holes shrinking to curves on the boundary (slits), and holes located at the end of thin tubes attached to the domain. We illustrate the accuracy of the results with numerical simulations, and extend them to higher dimensions.

Jun Zhou, Jiamin He
Thermoelastic suspension bridges operate under strong thermo-mechanical coupling, and the classical Fourier law fails to capture the finite speed of thermal propagation observed in low-conductivity materials such as concrete. This paper investigates a suspension bridge model in which the heat flux is governed by the Cattaneo law with relaxation time $τ$, and in which the bridge deck may or may not possess viscoelastic memory. Using operator semigroup theory, we establish well-posedness and derive sharp decay rates for both regimes. For the memoryless system ($δ=0$), we show that the semigroup is polynomially stable with rate $t^{-1/2}$ when the structural parameters satisfy $\frac{ρ_1}κ = \frac{ρ_2}{b}$, and that the rate deteriorates to $t^{-1/4}$ otherwise; moreover, exponential stability fails whenever $χ_0 \neq 0$, or $χ_0 = 0$ and $χ_1 = 0$, where $χ_0$ and $χ_1$ are parameter-dependent coefficients. In sharp contrast, when viscoelastic memory is present ($δ=1$), the semigroup becomes exponentially stable, regardless of the structural parameter ratio. This reveals a regularizing role of viscoelastic memory: it converts polynomial decay into exponential decay and removes the parameter-ratio obstruction. The results provide a theoretical basis for exploiting inherent viscoelasticity in long-span bridges and for optimizing deck parameters in memoryless structures.

The result is based on a discrete maximum principle, on $BV$ estimates of the approximated density, and on the characterization of the limit as entropy solution in the sense of Kru\v zkov.
♻ ☆ Mixed local-nonlocal equations with critical nonlinearity on $\mathbb{R}^N$: Non-existence, Existence, and Multiplicity of positive solutions

We consider the following quasilinear critical problem involving the mixed local-nonlocal operator: \begin{equation}\label{main_prob_abstract_1}\tag{$\mathcal{P}_p$} -Δ_p u+(-Δ_p)^s u=|u|^{p^*-2}u+f \text{ in }\mathbb{R}^N, \end{equation} where $s \in (0,1), p \in (1, \infty), N>p$, $p^*=\frac{Np}{N-p}$, and $f$ is a nonnegative functional in the dual space of the ambient solution space. If $f \equiv0$, then we show that \eqref{main_prob_abstract_1} does not admit any nontrivial weak solution. This phenomenon stands in contrast to the purely local and purely nonlocal cases. On the other hand, if $f$ is a nontrivial nonnegative functional, we establish the existence of a positive weak solution to \eqref{main_prob_abstract_1} provided $\|f\|$ is small. For this purpose we prove the concentration compactness principle for the mixed operator $-Δ_p +(-Δ_p)^s$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. We also discuss the multiplicity of positive weak solutions to \eqref{main_prob_abstract_1}.

The Anderson tight-binding model is a fundamental model of quantum transport and localization in disordered media. The proof uses the multiscale framework of Fröhlich-Spencer and Bourgain-Kenig, and the main new ingredient is a probabilistic discrete unique continuation principle (PDUC) for the discrete Schrödinger equation. ♻ ☆ On the dispersive estimates for the discrete Schrödinger equation on a honeycomb lattice
Younghun Hong, Yukihide Tadano, Changhun Yang
The discrete Schrödinger equation on a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice is a fundamental tight-binding approximation model that describes the propagation of waves on graphene. For free evolution, we first show that the degenerate frequencies of the dispersion relation are completely characterized by three symmetric periodic curves (Theorem 2.1), and that the three curves meet at Dirac points where conical singularities appear (see Figure 2.1). Based on this observation, we prove the $L^1\to L^\infty$ dispersion estimates for the linear flow depending on the frequency localization (Theorem 2.3). Collecting all, we obtain the dispersion estimate with $O(|t|^{-2/3})$ decay as well as Strichartz estimates. As an application, we prove small data scattering for a nonlinear model (Theorem 2.10). The proof of the key dispersion estimates is based on the associated oscillatory integral estimates with degenerate phases and conical singularities at Dirac points. Our proof is direct and uses only elementary methods.

♻ ☆ Continuous sonic-supersonic flows in two-dimensional infinitely long divergent nozzles
Lili Qian, Chunpeng Wang, Zihao Zhang
This paper concerns continuous sonic-supersonic flows in a two-dimensional infinitely long divergent nozzle with straight solid walls. For a given inlet that is a small perturbation of an arc centered at the vertex of the nozzle, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of a continuous sonic-supersonic potential flow which is close to the radially symmetric sonic-supersonic flow. The flow is sonic at the inlet, with its velocity along the normal direction, and becomes supersonic in the nozzle. Such a sonic-supersonic model is governed by a quasilinear nonstrictly hyperbolic equation with degeneracy at the inlet, and the degeneracy is weak in the sense that there exist exactly two distinct characteristics from each sonic point, except for those at the walls, pointing into the supersonic region. One of the crucial ingredients of the analysis is to obtain the precise asymptotic behavior near the sonic inlet by the method of characteristics, which is essential for establishing the local existence of continuous sonic-supersonic flows. Another one is to extend the local solution globally and derive uniform estimates in the supersonic region.
♻ ☆ A minimization problem for a cooperative system with a degenerate Bernoulli weight
Lili Du, Chunlei Yang, Jing Yang
In this paper, we study local minimizers of the energy functional$J(\mathbf{u}) = \int_D (|\nabla \mathbf{u}|^2 + Q^2(x)χ_{Ω_{\mathbf{u}}})\,dx$ which give rise to a singular cooperative system. Here \(\mathbf{u}=(u_1,\dots,u_m): D\to\R_+^m\) is a vector-valued unknown function, \(Ω_{\mathbf{u}}:=\{|\mathbf{u}|>0\}\) is the positive set, \(χ_{Ω_{\mathbf{u}}}\) is the characteristic function of the positive set \(Ω_{\mathbf{u}}\), and \(Q(x)\) is the Bernoulli weight function. This problem was first introduced by Caffarelli, Shahgholian, and Yeressian in the poineer work ({\it Duke Math. J.} \textbf{167}(10), 2018), where the regularity theory for minimizers and for the free boundary \(\partialΩ_{\mathbf{u}}\) was established for nondegenerate Bernoulli weights, i.e., \(Q(x)\ge Q_{\rm min}>0\). The present paper studies the same free boundary problem but for a degenerate Bernoulli weight. The main difficulty lies in the coupling between the degeneracy of \(Q(x)\) and the vector-valued nature of the problem. We show that the the free boundary set \(\partialΩ_{\mathbf{u}}\cap\{Q(x)=0\}\) decomposes into a nondegenerate part and a degenerate part. Nondegenerate points admit nontrivial blow-up limits; degenerate points have zero weighted density. We classify nondegenerate points into single-phase, multi-phase non-branching, and multi-phase branching points, analyzing their geometric structure. The branching-point singular structure for multi-phase points is purely vectorial and new in this setting. Finally, following Naber--Valtorta (Ann. Math. 185, 2017) and Edelen--Engelstein (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 371, 2019), we prove the nondegenerate set has locally finite $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-measure and is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable.

Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with nonpositive sectional curvature and smooth bounded geometry. If such a surface is even asymptotically hyperbolic, the $L^2\to L^q$ spectral estimates on complete nontrapped geodesics, for $q>2$, gain the square root of the window width. The high-frequency Schrödinger estimate holds for all times on these surfaces, both on compact segments and on complete nontrapped geodesics. Under a regularity assumption at the spectral threshold, the all-time estimate holds on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace.
♻ ☆ Vanishing boundary geometry and critical pressure compactness for the three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations

We prove boundary partial regularity for the three-dimensional nonstationary Navier--Stokes equations in bounded domains with fractional Sobolev boundary graphs whose integrability exponent is greater than three. Within the fractional Sobolev graph setting, this lowers the boundary threshold from fifteen quarters to three. We work in Breit's boundary suitable weak-solution framework, with the mixed maximal-regularity pair $(5/3,15/14)$ explicitly included in the solution assumptions. The main difficulty is to recover pressure compactness without imposing higher regularity on the rough boundary coefficients. After a rigid rotation to the tangent plane and parabolic rescaling, we show that each boundary graph becomes small in both Sobolev multiplier classes needed for the local energy inequality and the critical Stokes estimate. Geometry and fluid excess enter a contradiction argument as independent small parameters, so the limiting problem is the standard flat Stokes system. A localized pressure decomposition separates the vanishing nonlinear and coefficient errors from the forced and homogeneous flat pressures. The error pressure converges strongly at the critical mixed integrability pair, whereas higher spatial integrability is used only for the flat problems. These estimates yield a one-step excess decay bound with a constant independent of the contraction radius. A physical-scale iteration, followed by interior--boundary Campanato patching, gives local parabolic Hölder continuity of the velocity at every regular boundary point when the force has integrability exponent greater than five halves. The boundary singular set is relatively closed and has zero parabolic Hausdorff measure in dimension five thirds. The geometric decay determines a uniform starting scale and does not restrict the final regularity exponent.

We are interested in the asymptotic behavior of solutions toward strong rarefaction waves for a parabolic-hyperbolic system arising from chemotaxis. Suppose that the Riemann problem to the corresponding inviscid system admits rarefaction waves. We show that if the initial data is a small perturbation of an approximate rarefaction wave, then the Cauchy problem has a unique global solution that converges to the rarefaction wave asymptotically in time. The stability results hold regardless of the wave strengths. The waves can be either a single rarefaction wave or a composite of two rarefaction waves. In the composite case, we separate the initial centers of the two approximate profiles to make their interaction error term small while retaining convergence to the prescribed Riemann wave. The proofs are based on the energy method, where the key observations are the monotonicity of the approximate rarefaction waves with respect to both space and time, and the appropriate replacement of spatial derivative of the hyperbolic component with the parabolic component in proper forms.

☆ Kadison duality for biaffinely convex sets
Tea Štrekelj
Classical Kadison duality establishes a categorical equivalence between compact convex sets and Archimedean order unit spaces of affine functions. This paper develops a Kadison-type duality for sets with coordinate-wise convex structure in product domains $\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^m$. While slice-wise convex (biconvex) sets appear to be the natural geometric domain, separate convexity along coordinates is insufficient to ensure separation by biaffine polynomials. In classical convexity, every closed convex set is determined by affine functionals because any exterior point can be separated by a hyperplane. In contrast, biaffine polynomials can only probe a biconvex set $K$ up to its biaffine hull biconv$(K)$, the envelope formed by the intersection of all regions cut out by valid biaffine inequalities on $K$. To resolve this obstruction, the geometric setting is restricted to biaffinely convex sets, those that coincide with their biaffine hull ($K =$ biconv$(K)$) and therefore admit strict biaffine separation. On the algebraic side, we introduce the dual objects, which we call biaffine order unit spaces. These are finite-dimensional Archimedean order unit spaces defined on tensor products $E_1 \otimes E_2$ whose order units factor and whose positive cones are governed entirely by unentangled, rank-1 tensor evaluations. We prove a duality between the category of compact non-degenerate biaffinely convex sets with coordinate-wise affine maps and the category of abstract biaffine order unit spaces with tensor-factorized unital positive linear maps. In particular, every such biaffinely convex set is isomorphic to the coordinate state space of its biaffine polynomials, and conversely, every biaffine order unit space is order-isomorphic to the space of biaffine polynomials on its coordinate state space.

☆ Non-expansive maps between unit balls that send the sphere onto the sphere are linear isometries

Let $X$, $Y$ be real Banach spaces with closed unit balls $B_X$, $B_Y$ and unit spheres $S_X$, $S_Y$. We prove that every non-expansive map $F\colon B_X\to B_Y$ with $F(S_X)\subseteq S_Y\subseteq F(B_X)$ is the restriction of a surjective linear isometry $X\to Y$. Consequently, a non-expansive bijection of $B_X$ onto itself that fails to be an isometry must map some point of $S_X$ into the open unit ball, so the plasticity of $B_X$ reduces to showing that non-expansive bijections preserve norm 1. The proof shows that $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at $0$ with a surjective linear isometry $T$ as its derivative, and then proves $T^{-1}F=\mathrm{id}$ using a quantitative rigidity lemma for non-expansive self-maps $H$ of $B_X$ satisfying $\|a+H(a)\|=2$ for $a\in S_X$; the latter relies on the Baillon-Bruck rate of asymptotic regularity for Krasnosel'skii-Mann iterations. As a corollary, the identity is extremal in the set of non-expansive self-maps of $B_X$ for every Banach space $X$, which together with a result of Bargetz, Dymond and Pirk shows that all surjective isometries of $B_X$ are extremal, answering a question of theirs, including the case of $L^1[0,1]$.

Grégoire Szymanski, Fabrice Wunderlich
Aldous' criterion provides a stopping-time characterisation of tightness in Skorokhod's $J_1$ topology and is one of the standard tools for proving functional limit theorems. For the weaker $M_1$ topology, where limiting jumps can be approximated by clustered jumps or steep continuous motion, no analogous characterisation has been available and tightness classically requires controlling a global oscillation modulus over all nearby triples of times. We prove such an Aldous-type characterisation of $M_1$ tightness, replacing the global modulus condition by local estimates at stopping times ruling out rapid reversals after a large excursion. Together with the standard compact containment and boundary conditions, these estimates are both necessary and sufficient for $M_1$ tightness. As a consequence, we derive tractable and general sufficient conditions for additive functionals of strong Markov processes. They reduce the verification of $M_1$ tightness to short-time estimates for the processes restarted from its state at suitable stopping times.

☆ Kirszbraun's Intersection Property and Nonexpansive Extensions
Valentin Gutev
This paper aims to present the historical development of the extension problem of nonexpansive maps in Euclidean and Hilbert spaces, and to serve as a comprehensive guide to this specific area. Such extensions are based on a geometric property of the intersection of closed balls in Euclidean spaces, known as the Kirszbraun intersection property. Subsequently, a number of authors have extended this property to Hilbert and other spaces. All these results are discussed in this paper, but the paper itself is not a mechanical compilation of already known proofs. The material has been developed with an emphasis on the natural connections between all these results and the corresponding concepts involved in them. Furthermore, most of these results are presented with new simplified proofs. Last but not least, the paper also contains some new results related to this extension problem.

We study first-order locally convex Lie algebroids in the setting of Bastiani calculus. The first-order condition is automatic in finite rank, but is an additional regularity hypothesis for general locally convex vector bundles. We define sheaves of scalar-valued and vector-valued Lie algebroid forms as fiberwise continuous alternating maps with smooth local representatives. Morphisms are defined by requiring the induced pullback on inverse-image sheaves of scalar-valued forms to commute with the Lie algebroid differentials. We prove that these algebroids form a category, study representations and cohomology sheaves, and show that the Lie algebroids and morphisms of locally convex Lie groupoids belong to this category. We also give two applications. For a compact manifold $K$, the current algebroid $C^\infty(K,A)\to C^\infty(K,M)$ of a first-order Banach Lie algebroid $A\to M$ is a first-order Fréchet Lie algebroid, provided $M$ admits local addition. Finally, we prove a Banach Lie II theorem: a morphism from the Lie algebroid of a locally convex Lie groupoid to that of a Banach-Lie groupoid, both with Hausdorff source fibers, integrates uniquely to a groupoid morphism when the source groupoid is source-connected and source-simply connected.

En route, we prove corresponding entropy inequalities under the quadratic optimal transport coupling, including an entropy power inequality for the minimum and maximum in Euclidean space. We also study the stability of four-function inequalities under convolution with log-concave product densities, recovering the preservation of log-supermodularity established by Karlin and Rinott, and explain its application to a conditional entropy power inequality for log-supermodular random variables.

We also showed that, as expected, a more restrictive condition is required to characterize the almost surely separated Poisson processes with the same first intensity as $Λ_φ$. To gain further insight into this difference in behavior, we focus on radial weights $φ$ and introduce a hybrid process $Λ_φ^M=\{r_j e^{iθ_j}\}_{j}$, where the moduli $r_j$ are taken from $Λ_φ$, while the arguments $θ_j$ are chosen independently and uniformly in $[0,2π)$, independently of the radii. Our main result is that the hybrid process is almost surely separated under exactly the same condition as the corresponding Poisson process. Thus, despite preserving the joint radial distribution of the determinantal process, independent angular randomization destroys its improved separation properties.

Previsions are positively homogeneous functionals, and are generalized forms of integration functionals. We investigate previsions -- just previsions, not sublinear or superlinear previsions as in previous work. This extends to homeomorphisms between spaces of previsions and certain hyperspaces over spaces of sublinear or superlinear previsions, which can also be characterized in terms of orthogonality relations, making the construction a variant of a double powerspace construction.

♻ ☆ Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
Eduardo Dueñez, José Iovino
This is the first of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on stability. An observable is stable when the order in which the two systems are idealized never changes its expectation value, and this is Shelah's stability. Its classical characterizations, in model theory and in analysis, acquire a physical meaning: idealized preparations are simulated by finite mixtures of actual ones, and adaptive probes can tell apart only polynomially many preparations.

For $\mathcal H:\mathcal B^α\to\mathcal B^α_{\log}$, we determine the exact norm: it is equal to $3/2$ for $1<α\leq4/3$ and is given by an explicit Gamma-function formula for $4/3<α<2$. We also determine the exact norm of $\mathcal H:H^1\to H^1_{\log}$ and show that it is equal to $π$. Finally, for $0<α<1$, we determine the exact norm of $\mathcal H:H^\infty_α\to\mathcal B^{α+1}$, which is given by an explicit Gamma-function formula.

We study a class of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) with jumps modeling multistage Michaelis--Menten enzyme kinetics, in which a substrate is sequentially transformed into a product via a cascade of intermediate complexes. These networks are typically high-dimensional and exhibit multiscale behavior with a strong coupling between different components, posing substantial analytical and computational challenges. In particular, the problem of statistical inference of reaction rates is significantly difficult and becomes even more intricate when direct observations of system states are unavailable and only a random sample of product formation times is observed. We address this problem in two stages. First, in a suitable scaling regime consistent with the Quasi-Steady State Approximation (QSSA), we rigorously establish a stochastic averaging principle yielding a reduced model for the product-substrate dynamics. Guided by the reduced-order dynamics, we next construct a novel Interacting Particle System (IPS) that approximates the product-substrate process at the particle level. This IPS plays a pivotal role in the inference methodology, and we prove several non-asymptotic bounds and limiting results for this system. These results facilitate the construction of an estimator based on a product-form approximate likelihood requiring only a random sample of product formation times. This approach does not need access to the system states, and we rigorously prove consistency of the estimator.

We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by Tartar's vision of a \emph{point-free} theory, we derive explicit norm resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting technique and solve a generalized Sylvester equation that controls the commutator between the differential structure and the highly oscillatory material properties. This abstract perspective unifies stationary, non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions between these media--and their respective convergence rates--are entirely captured by the behavior of the spectral measures of the microscopic and macroscopic derivative operators near zero frequency.

☆ An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability
Alexander Rodriguez, Benjamin Palacios
We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.

We investigate refined large-time propagation and front interaction in a two-species Lotka--Volterra competition--diffusion system on the real line. When the faster competitor spreads into unoccupied habitat, its invasion front generates a moving heterogeneous environment for the trailing competitor, whose front position may be influenced by the leading front's Bramson delay. We first study a scalar Fisher--KPP equation in a shifting environment. Under weighted integrability assumptions on the growth profile, we determine the logarithmic front corrections up to a bounded error and identify the corresponding limiting wave profiles, thereby explicitly demonstrating how the logarithmic displacement of the environment modifies the classical Bramson correction. The resulting asymptotics distinguish locally pulled propagation, nonlocal pulling, and two critical transition regimes. In the forced-wave regime, the invasion front remains locked to the moving environment, and the dynamics select a unique stationary profile from a one-parameter family. In the nonlocal pulling regime, the favourable habitat ahead accelerates the invasion front even though the front lags behind the environmental shift. At the threshold of nonlocal pulling, the interaction modifies only the logarithmic correction and, at a further critical parameter value, produces an additional $\ln\ln t$ term. We then apply these results to the competition system. In the nonlocally pulled regime, we determine the logarithmic displacement of the trailing invasion front, explicitly quantifying the transmission of the leading species' Bramson delay, and prove convergence to the corresponding travelling-wave profile. Finally, we establish a Liouville-type rigidity principle for a class of monotone parabolic systems. This yields uniqueness of monostable travelling waves in both competition regimes.

Math., 2022) to a sharp improved inequality at the critical order $s=\frac{n}{2}$ under arbitrary finite-order moment constraints. We further investigate the best remainder constant. Math., 2018), where the best remainder vanishes, we show that it is positive in several higher-dimensional regimes. In this paper, we study the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier--Stokes equations with the Coriolis force in the half space with the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We show the existence of a unique small solution in the scale-critical Besov spaces. In particular, for any boundary data with only the normal component assumed to be sufficiently small, and for any external forces, we establish the well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary value problem when the speed of rotation is sufficiently large. In the proof, to exploit the stabilizing effect of the Coriolis term, we employ two explicit formulas depending on the relation between the horizontal frequency and the magnitude of the rotation speed.

☆ Blow-up of damped semilinear wave equation with short range potential and critical power nonlinearity
Ikeda Masahiro, Tu Ziheng, Wang Chengbo
The present paper is devoted to the study of a semilinear wave equation with spatially dependent scattering damping and a short-range potential, with particular focus on determining the critical exponent for the power-type nonlinearity. By employing the test function method, we establish wave-type blow-up results and derive lifespan estimates at the critical level. The main contribution of this work lies in providing a uniform asymptotic analysis for a family of test functions, which is achieved through a detailed investigation of a parametric second-order elliptic equation. As a further novelty, we relax the radial symmetry condition conventionally imposed on the coefficients $D$ and $V$ by resorting to the comparison principle in conjunction with a monotone exhaustion argument.
☆ Structural stability of cylindrical transonic shocks to the three-dimensional Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring combustion equations
Zihao Zhang, Yan Zhou
We address the structural stability of transonic shock solutions to the Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring (ZND) combustion equations in a cylindrical domain under three-dimensional perturbations of the incoming supersonic flow and exit pressure. The perturbed transonic shock is completely free and its strength and position are uniquely determined by the incoming flow and the exit pressure. The solution shares the same regularity for the velocity, the pressure, the entropy and the fraction of unburned gas. The main difficulties are that the shock front is a free boundary to be determined simultaneously with the subsonic flow and the equations for all states are coupled with each other due to the combustion process. One of the key ingredients of the analysis is to reformulate the three-dimensional ZND combustion equations into a deformation-curl system and four transport equations in terms of the deformation tensor and vorticity. Another one is an elaborate decomposition of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions so that the shock front is uniquely determined by an algebraic equation and an unusual second order differential boundary condition is obtained on the shock front for the first order nonlocal deformation-curl system, from which an oblique boundary condition can be derived after homogenizing the curl system and introducing the potential function.

We develop a pinching method for mean curvature flow in higher codimension. Motivated by pinching constructions for Ricci flow, the method uses a nonlinear deformation of the second fundamental form. We introduce two tensorial curvature conditions for closed immersions in Euclidean space which extend beyond the scope of classical scalar pinching results. In dimensions at least ten, we apply the method to prove convergence to a round point under the first condition and a canonical neighborhood theorem under the second.

We address the question of global in time existence for the semilinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} \partial_t u-Δu&=&|u|^{b-1}u \quad {\rm ~in~} \mathbb{R}^n\times (0,\infty),\\ u(\cdot,0)&=& u_0 \quad {\rm ~in~} \mathbb{R}^n, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $b> 1+2/n, n\geq 1$. We found a space of initial data $Z$ that guarantees the existence of a global in time solution whenever the norm of the initial datum $u_0$ in $Z$ is small. The space $Z$ is optimal in the sense that if $u_0$ is a nonnegative distribution and the equation admits a nonnegative solution $u\in L^b_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty))$, then $u_0\in Z$. Moreover, our result contains all of the known results in the literature. In particular, it implies that global in time existence does hold for end-point Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces, which resolves an open problem posed by L. Brandolese and F. Cortez (J. Funct. Anal. $\textbf{276}$ (2019), 2589-2604).

☆ Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
Ricardo Freire, Cristian González-Riquelme, Claudio Muñoz, Felipe Poblete, Vicente Salinas
Let $χ_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,χ_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $ξ_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, Φ_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du, \] where $Φ_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ Φ_L(u) := \frac{1}{2π}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} ξ_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $ξ_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $Λ_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge Λ_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $Λ_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $Λ_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $Λ_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $Λ_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH by Platt and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.

☆ Monomial Moving Zeros for the Heat Semigroup: An Explicit Finite-Order Differential Hierarchy
Gerardo Hernandez-del-Valle
Let $P_t=\exp(t\D^2/2)$ be the heat semigroup. For every integer $k\geq2$ and parameter $ρ\in\C$, we construct an entire function $Γ_{ρ,k}$ whose heat evolution has the prescribed moving zero $x=ρt^k$ and constant spatial flux there: \[ (P_tΓ_{ρ,k})(ρt^k)=0, \qquad \partial_x(P_tΓ_{ρ,k})(ρt^k)=1. \] The initial function is explicit, \[ Γ_{ρ,k}(x) =x\sum_{q\geq0}\frac{(-2^kρx^{2k-1})^q}{q!} \frac{(kq)!}{((2k-1)q+1)!}, \] and is a generalized hypergeometric function whose entire-function order is strictly below two. Most importantly, it is annihilated by an explicit polynomial-coefficient differential operator of order $2k-1$. Thus every monomial moving boundary admits a finite-order stationary realization after a natural boundary-flux selection, even though the naive order-$k$ family $\D^k+a x^{k-1}$ already fails to produce the exact boundary at $k=4$. No minimality claim is made: the result gives a universal finite-order hierarchy, while the least possible differential order remains open and depends on the choice made inside the inverse kernel.

We describe the $L^p$-parabolicity of a Riemannian manifold in terms of a unified theory of nonlinear $L^p$-capacities, for the whole range $1\leq p\leq \infty$. For example, the \(L^{1}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to the usual notion of parabolicity/recurrence, while \(L^{2}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to biparabolicity. For any $1\leq p\leq \infty,$ the $L^p$-parabolicity turns out to be equivalent to the $L^q$-Liouville property for positive superharmonic functions, where $p$ and $q$ are Hölder conjugate exponents. We also provide a new capacitary characterization of the $L^1$-Liouville property. Finally we obtain an almost optimal volume growth condition for the $L^p$-parabolicity for $1

☆ Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy
Ihsan Topaloglu
We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.

☆ A Brezis--Merle inequality for the biharmonic operator with Dirichlet boundary conditions in four-dimensional balls
João Marcos do Ó, Federica Sani, Victor Rafael Silva
In this paper, we establish a Brezis-Merle type inequality for very weak solutions of the biharmonic Dirichlet problem in the four-dimensional unit ball. By combining this inequality with moving-plane arguments, we obtain uniform a priori estimates for positive solutions of semilinear biharmonic equations with exponential nonlinearities in both the subcritical and critical regimes. As an application of these estimates, we prove the existence of a positive solution by means of topological methods. We also extend the analysis to a class of non-variational cooperative systems.

☆ Low Residuals, Wrong Value: Learning the Viscosity Solution of Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs Equations with PINNs
Raul Jimenez, Pablo Tejerina-Pérez, Leonid Sarieddine, Pedro Tarancón-Álvarez, Marisol Traforetti, Pau Solé-Vilaró, Oleksii Ignatenko, Nazar Tkach, Pavlos Protopapas
Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other residual-trained solvers judge a candidate solution by the size of its sampled PDE residual. For first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations this is not sufficient: the same equation and boundary data admit Lipschitz almost-everywhere solutions that differ from the viscosity solution by $O(1)$ while violating the equation only on sets of measure zero. We study whether residual minimization selects such solutions in a fixed-horizon pursuit-evasion game whose Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs value function is known in closed form on the circle $S^1$ and on the flat tori $\mathbb{T}^{2}$ and $\mathbb{T}^{4}$. We train four neural parameterizations with ten seeds on each geometry, 120 runs in total. A standard network with periodic Fourier features converges to folded almost-everywhere solutions in all 30 runs: small residuals and the expected capture-layer gradient, yet values that are wrong over most of the domain. A network with periodicity imposed through the loss recovers the viscosity solution in one and two dimensions but becomes unreliable in four. Two parameterizations that receive the geodesic distance do substantially better: a single network fed the wrapped displacement and its distance recovers the viscosity solution in all 30 runs, while a minimum over periodic image charts succeeds in 27 of 30 and introduces a wrong-image failure mode. Finally, for the convex Hamiltonian considered here, we use the semiconcavity of the viscosity solution to build a mesh-free finite-difference test that needs only forward network evaluations; it detects the folded solutions and the harmful min-of-charts failures without access to the exact value function. A small sampled residual thus does not by itself validate a learned Hamilton-Jacobi solution; the parameterization and independent structural diagnostics can be essential for selecting the viscosity solution.

☆ Structure-Preserving Numerical Schemes for a Time-Fractional Porous Medium Equation with Nonlocal Pressure
Łukasz Płociniczak, Hubert Woszczek
In this work, we study numerical approximations of the equation \begin{equation} \partial_t^αu-\nabla\cdot\left(u^{m-1}\nabla(-Δ)^{-σ}u\right)=0, \end{equation} where $0<α<1$, $0<σ<1$ and $m>1$. The Caputo derivative is discretized by the L1 formula, while the nonlinear nonlocal flux is approximated by a conservative upwind finite-difference scheme. We establish several structural properties of the implicit scheme in arbitrary space dimension, including a discrete maximum principle, non-negativity, mass conservation, $\ell^\infty$ and $\ell^2$ stability, existence of non-negative discrete solutions, and a discrete energy-dissipation estimate. Our assumptions include natural symmetry, a sign condition on the sum of the directional coefficients, and decay on the discrete weights. We also derive a consistency estimate for the complete nonlinear spatial operator. For rigorous convergence analysis, we restrict ourselves to one space dimension and introduce the cumulative variable associated with the density. This transforms the discrete problem into a monotone approximation of an equation involving the fractional Laplacian. Interestingly, for semigroup-based pressure-gradient weights, the resulting discrete operator is identified with the fractional discrete Laplacian. Next, using comparison and contraction properties of the integrated scheme, for $m\geq2$ and under the stated spatial regularity and weighted temporal consistency assumptions, we prove uniform convergence of the cumulative numerical solution and convergence of the corresponding density against compactly supported smooth test functions. The temporal estimates allow a weak singularity at the initial time. We also analyze an explicit variant of the scheme and derive a sufficient CFL condition covering the full range $0<σ<1$.
☆ Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
Vitalii Shpakivskyi
A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.
♻ ☆ A counterexample to Kenig's conjecture for the Laplace double-layer operator
Matthew J. Colbrook, Siavash Sadeghi
We disprove Kenig's 1994 spectral-radius conjecture for the double-layer operator in every dimension $d\ge2$. For every $t>1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, we construct a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with connected boundary such that the double-layer operator on $L^2$ with respect to the surface measure has $\pm \mathrm{i} t$ in its Fredholm essential spectrum. In particular, the essential spectral radius is greater than $1/2$. In the plane, the boundary may be chosen differentiable everywhere and smooth away from a single point. Our planar construction develops a refinement mechanism that produces unbounded growth of adjoint resolvent solutions with fixed forcing while keeping the graph slopes uniformly bounded. A closed recursion for the density and its image under an auxiliary singular integral reduces the growth estimate to a certified inequality for Hermitian $2\times2$ matrices. The certificate uses continuous estimates, exact rational arithmetic and rigorous interval enclosures. Localisation and rescaled graph insertions then produce a weakly null sequence of normalised approximate eigenvectors for the adjoint double-layer operator on one bounded boundary. A compact intertwining relation on Cartesian products of the planar domain with cubes gives the higher-dimensional examples without changing the spectral parameter.
♻ ☆ Solutions to Monge-Ampère Equations with Low Codimensional singularities

We construct solutions to Monge-Ampère equations whose Monge-Ampère measures contain singular components supported on low codimensional sets. We also study the regularity of such solutions. To motivate our construction, we present examples arising from optimal transport where the potential of optimal transport maps satisfy Monge-Ampère equations similar to the ones we study.

♻ ☆ Stability of 3D Stratified Plane Couette Flow: A New Lift-up Mechanism and Potential Vorticity
Yiting Yao
Since the pioneering work of Taylor and Goldstein in 1931 laid the foundation for the study of parallel stratified shear flows, non-parallel configurations have received comparatively little attention. We study the stability of the 3D Boussinesq system near the plane Couette flow $V^*=(y,0,0)$ under the vertically stratified background $η^*=αz$. The shear and stratification directions are perpendicular. This geometry produces two structural effects that are absent in the parallel configuration: an additional nonlocal coupling in the non-zero-mode system, which obstructs a directly useful symmetrization, and a wave-shear coupled lift-up mechanism for the zero modes. The $L^p$ transient growth due to the lift-up effect can be suppressed either by sufficiently strong stratification (for $p>2$) or under suitable assumptions on the initial data (for $p\geq 2$). To study the nonzero-mode system, we introduce a reformulation based on the linearized potential vorticity (PV), a fundamental quantity in geophysical fluid dynamics, to recover a better energy structure. We establish the inviscid damping of $u_{1,\neq}$ and $u_{2,\neq}$. We further apply the linearized PV formulation to study the linear stability of the tilted Couette flow. Finally, we use this formulation to prove the nonlinear stability for perturbations on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$.

Guoqing Cui, Chong Gu, Nam Q. Le, Ling Wang, Bin Zhou
We establish interior and global Hölder estimates for linearized Monge-Ampère equations in divergence form in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, when the Hessian determinant of the convex Monge-Ampère potential is bounded above and below by positive constants and the vector field on the right-hand side is bounded. The estimates use the $L^p$ norm of the solution for any $p>1$. A key ingredient is an $L^1$ estimate, with appropriate decay rates, for the gradient of the Green's function of the linearized Monge-Ampère operator in small sections, uniform with respect to the pole. As applications, we obtain uniform Hölder estimates for the time derivatives of the primal and dual potentials in the three-dimensional periodic dual semigeostrophic system when the initial density is bounded away from zero and infinity, and establish a linear convergence rate for periodic homogenization of the Monge-Ampère equation.

♻ ☆ Spectrum of the wave equation with Dirac damping on a compact star graph
Mikuláš Kučera
We consider the wave equation with a distributional Dirac damping and Dirichlet boundary conditions on a compact interval. It is shown that the spectrum of the corresponding wave operator is fully determined by zeroes of an entire function. Consequently, a considerable change of spectral properties is shown for certain critical values of the damping parameter. We also derive a definitive criterion for the Riesz basis property of the root vectors for an arbitrary placement of a complex-valued Dirac damping. Finally, we consider a generalisation of the problem for compact star graphs and provide insight into the essence of the critical damping constant.

♻ ☆ An inverse free boundary problem
Cătălin I. Cârstea, Matti Lassas, Jinpeng Lu, Lauri Oksanen, Ziyao Zhao
We study inverse problems for the elliptic and parabolic obstacle problems from boundary measurements. For the classical elliptic obstacle problem with strictly superharmonic obstacle function, we show that the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map admits a one-sided linearization at every boundary datum lying strictly above the obstacle. The linearized map is the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a rough Dirichlet problem on the a priori unknown non-contact set. We show that these linearized Cauchy data uniquely determine the non-contact set up to set of Sobolev $2$-capacity zero and consequently determine the obstacle. Our result applies to the inverse problem for a parabolic obstacle problem where both the coefficient and the obstacle function are time-independent by reducing to the elliptic inverse problem.

♻ ☆ On the Cauchy problem for the Tzitzéica equation: Soliton resolution conjecture and asymptotic analysis
Shou-Fu Tian, Jia-Fu Tong
We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitzéica equation, which is an important integrable model arising in affine differential geometry and characterizing proper affine spheres. Recently, Huang, Wang and Zhu (Math. Ann. \textbf{395}, 18 (2026)) reported the long-time asymptotic result for the Tzitzéica equation with purely continuous spectrum. Inspired by their work, we carry out a full asymptotic analysis of the Tzitzéica equation. Compared with the previous work, by developing the $\bar{\partial}$-nonlinear steepest descent method, we reveal that the solutions of the Tzitzéica equation exhibits three different asymptotic regions depending on $ξ:=x/t$. For the region $ξ\in(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$, where there are no stationary phase points, we rigorously prove that the solution satisfies $u(x,t)=O_ξ(t^{-1})$ for $ξ\ge1$ and $u(x,t)=2πi+O_ξ(t^{-1})$ for $ξ\le-1$. In the region $ξ\in(-1,1)$, the phase function $θ(z)$ has two stationary phase points. The corresponding asymptotic approximations can be characterized with an $N$-soliton solution as well as an interaction term between soliton solutions and the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_K})$ with $0\le b_K<1/4$. In the transition regions $\{(x,t):1-\varepsilon<|ξ|<1\}$, the corresponding asymptotic approximation can be characterized by the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_\varepsilon})$ where $0\le b_\varepsilon<1/4$. Our results provide a rigorous analysis of the long-time asymptotic behavior of solutions of the Tzitzéica equation in different regions and confirm the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitzéica equation.

♻ ☆ Fully localised three-dimensional solitary water waves on Beltrami flows with strong surface tension
Mark D. Groves, Erik Wahlén
Fully localised three-dimensional solitary waves are steady water waves which are evanescent in every horizontal direction. This paper presents an existence theory for such waves under the assumptions that the relative vorticity and velocity fields are parallel (`Beltrami flows'), that the free surface of the water takes the form $\{z=η(x,y)\}$ for some function $η: {\mathbb R}^2\rightarrow{\mathbb R}$, and that the influence of surface tension is sufficiently strong. The governing equations are formulated as a single equation for $η$, which is then reduced to a perturbation of the KP-I equation. This equation has recently been shown to have a family of nondegenerate localised solutions, and an application of a suitable variant of the implicit-function theorem shows that they persist under perturbations.
♻ ☆ The quantitative isoperimetric inequality: A calibration argument
Sebastian Hensel, Tim Laux
We give a short proof of the quantitative isoperimetric inequality. Our argument is based on a notion of quantitative calibrations which induce a natural distance controlling both the Fraenkel asymmetry and the tilt excess. The proof of our key result which can be viewed as a nonlinear, geometric version of Fuglede's result in $BV$ is direct and self-contained. In particular, we do not make any use of regularity theory for almost minimizers.

♻ ☆ Energy minimizers in a periodic phase transition model of light-matter interaction in nematic liquid crystals
Panayotis Smyrnelis, Marcel G. Clerc, Manuel Diaz-Zuniga, Michał Kowalczyk
In this paper we complete the study of global minimizers of a forced, non autonomous, one dimensional, phase transition model, initiated in [8]. Motivated by the recent findings in [9], revealing new configurations of topological structures in light, we consider a forcing term having two periods. We show that depending on the strength of the forcing, at most two thresholds that determine the structure of the minimizers (kinks) are attained. These kinks are now a combination of three types observed experimentally, and they may have at most three zeros. The existence of these complex types of phase transition follows from a periodic one dimensional model of matter-light interaction in nematic liquid crystal based on a thin sample limit of the Oseen-Frank energy. We show that the qualitative behaviour of global minimizers is consistent with the original model.

♻ ☆ Convexity preservation for first-order nonlinear evolution equations with Neumann-type boundary conditions
Daowen Lin, Qing Liu
We study preservation of spatial convexity for viscosity solutions of first order Hamilton-Jacobi evolution equations with Neumann-type boundary conditions in bounded convex domains. Under a monotonicity assumption on the Hamiltonian in the outward normal direction, every viscosity supersolution of the Neumann problem is also a state-constraint supersolution. This reduces the boundary difficulty to a state-constraint problem and enables us to prove convexity preservation via the convex-envelope argument established by Alvarez, Lasry and Lions (1997). We also obtain propagation estimates for semiconvexity and strong convexity under similar structural assumptions.
♻ ☆ Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing small elastic particles
Juan Casado-Díaz, Antonio Rafael Hormigo-Molina
This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $γ=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size. For $γ=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $γ\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $γ\in(0,+\infty)$ and $γ=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $γ=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $γ\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.

♻ ☆ Existence and uniqueness of viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system
Sungho Han
We establish the existence and uniqueness, up to translation, of monotone viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system, provided the two end states satisfy the Rankine-Hugoniot and Lax entropy conditions and the shock strength is small. Taking the shock strength as a singular perturbation parameter, we reduce the profile equations by Fenichel's geometric singular perturbation theory to a scalar equation on a slow manifold and obtain the profile as a heteroclinic orbit. We also give pointwise estimates of the profiles and their derivatives up to fourth order, with explicit leading-order terms for the first derivatives.

Junior da Silva Bessa, Jehan Oh
In this paper we establish optimal $C^{1,α}$ regularity up to the boundary for viscosity solutions of fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy law and oblique boundary conditions. The approach developed here relies on first deriving uniform boundary Hölder estimates for perturbed models with oblique boundary data in ``almost $C^{1}$-flat'' domains. As a byproduct of our analysis, we determine the optimal Hölder exponent for solutions when the governing operator is quasiconvex or quasiconcave. In this paper, we treat the Fisher-KPP equation with a Caputo-type time fractional derivative and discuss the propagation speed of the solution. The equation is a mathematical model that describes the processes of sub-diffusion, proliferation, and saturation. We first consider a traveling wave solution to study the propagation of the solution, but we cannot define it in the usual sense due to the time fractional derivative in the equation. We therefore assume that the solution asymptotically approaches a traveling wave solution, and the asymptotic traveling wave solution is formally introduced as a potential asymptotic form of the solution. The existence and the properties of the asymptotic traveling wave solution are discussed using a monotone iteration method. Finally, the behavior of the solution is analyzed by numerical simulations based on the result for asymptotic traveling wave solutions.

♻ ☆ Resonant Microstructures as Dirac-type Sources for Acoustic Wave Control
Arpan Mukherjee, Mourad Sini
We study finite-time acoustic wave tracking using effective interior Dirac-type actuators generated by clusters of subwavelength resonant bubbles driven from exterior transducers. Starting from a time-domain point-interaction approximation, the full scattering problem is reduced to a finite-dimensional delayed system of interacting retarded monopoles. After localization to a bounded observation domain, we formulate the tracking problem on a prescribed finite-dimensional Dirichlet spectral subspace. At the ideal level, a full-rank spatial coupling condition yields exact tracking of arbitrary sufficiently smooth compatible trajectories in this subspace by interior point sources. These ideal actuators are realized using small, high-contrast bubbles, whose Laplace-domain transfer operator encodes the Minnaert resonances and collective attenuation. The principal mode of each cluster is isolated by the Perron--Frobenius structure and the intra-cluster spectral gap. Clusters tuned to the same band are then treated as a collective resonant block. The selected Dirichlet bands are matched with the corresponding Minnaert bands. For prescribed slowly time-modulated resonant pressure profiles, with sufficiently flat initialization, we construct causal exterior controls and obtain a quantitative tracking estimate on every fixed time interval $[0,T]$. In contrast, on frequency ranges uniformly separated from the Minnaert resonances, the actuator gain is $O(\varepsilon)$ and the corresponding realization cost is asymptotically unbounded as $\varepsilon \ll 1$, $\varepsilon$ being the maximum radius of the bubbles. Thus the Minnaert resonances convert accessible exterior excitations into robust effective interior controls.

♻ ☆ Weak solutions for weak turbulence models in electrostatic plasmas
Kun Huang, Irene M. Gamba
The weak turbulence model, also known as the quasilinear theory in plasma physics, has been a cornerstone in modeling resonant particle-wave interactions in plasmas. Stemming from the Vlasov-Poisson/Maxwell system under the weak turbulence assumption, incorporating the random phase approximation and ergodicity, it takes the form of a integro-differential system, which describes the time dynamics of particle distribution and wave spectrum. The interaction between particles and waves can be treated as a stochastic process, whose transition probability bridges the momentum space and the spectral space. To our knowledge, there is no preceding rigorous analytical work for the quasilinear theory addressed in this manuscript. In this paper, we establish the existence of global weak solutions to the one-dimensional electrostatic quasilinear model for nonnegative, smooth, rapidly decaying initial particle distributions and nonnegative, smooth wave spectra compactly supported in a positive wave-number band. The construction uses the resonance condition to reduce the coupled system to a scalar degenerate parabolic equation, together with uniform estimates and strong convergence of the gradients of regularized approximations. When the initial wave spectrum is positive throughout a single band, we further characterize the equilibrium selected by this approximation procedure. The equilibrium uniquely minimizes a quadratic functional over a nonnegative cone and admits a geometric construction through the least concave majorant of a primitive determined by the initial data. The limiting particle distribution is non-increasing on the corresponding resonant interval and forms plateaus wherever the equilibrium auxiliary function is positive. A relative-entropy argument establishes long-time convergence to this equilibrium.
♻ ☆ Stability of optimal transport maps and second variation of the 2-Monge-Kantorovich distance
F. -U. Caja-Lopez, Matias G. Delgadino, Jun Kitagawa
We establish several quantitative stability estimates for optimal transport maps between non-degenerate densities on uniformly convex domains for the quadratic cost. Under Hölder regularity assumptions, we prove Lipschitz $L^{2}$ (respectively $C^{0,α}$) stability estimates for optimal transport maps in terms of the $2$-Monge--Kantorovich distance (respectively $L^{p}$ distances) between pairs of source and target densities. When the continuity assumption is removed, we obtain a Lipschitz $L^{2}$ stability estimate for the Brenier potentials in terms of the $L^{2}$ distance between the source and target densities. The proofs rely on a precise characterization of the linear response of the Brenier potential along smooth interpolations of the data, obtained by linearizing the Monge--Ampère equation in divergence form. As a further application of this approach, we derive an explicit formula for the second variation of the quadratic Monge--Kantorovich distance.
